441	4. 阅读 [configs/miles/examples/README.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/examples/README.md) 的家族表（L8-L19）与 [docs/miles/olmo35-small.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/olmo35-small.md) 的 Recipe alignment 一节（L134-L150），用自己的话写三行：tiny 家族管什么、small 家族管什么、为什么 Small 计时不能直接沿用旧数字。
442	5. （可选，CPU 即可）按 olmo35-small.md 的资格检查流程把 two-node-mech 复制到被忽略的 `runs/` 后做规划：
443	
444	   ```bash
445	   mkdir -p runs && cp configs/miles/examples/small/two-node-mech.toml runs/small-mech.toml
446	   uv run python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/small-mech.toml
447	   ```
448	
449	**需要观察的现象**：步骤 1 中 small/ 下只有三份 B300 配方，`--diff-filter=D` 显示 `small/dev.toml` 在 92776a730（PR #2280）被删除；步骤 2 中六份示例全部 `calculate_per_token_loss = true`，grpo.md 的片段与 development-defaults 的措辞同为 token-mean；步骤 3 中 tiny/node 与 small/two-node-mech 的 `learning_rate`/`rollout_batch_size`/`global_batch_size` 完全一致（6e-6 / 256 / 2048）。
450	
451	**预期结果**：能复述两个家族的分工（Tiny 力学/学习示例 vs Small B300 实测配方）与共享的学习基线；步骤 1-4 为只读操作，可安全执行；步骤 5 的 `plan` 输出（含占位路径的 advisory）**待本地验证**——文档承诺规划无需 GPU，但本讲未实际运行。
452	
453	#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案
454	
455	**练习 1**：`tiny/` 与 `small/` 两个家族各自的分工是什么？为什么 Small 没有单 GPU 训练配方？
456	
457	**参考答案**：`tiny/` 是 Tiny 微型模型的力学检查（dev）与学习示例（node/three-node）；`small/` 是实测的 OLMo 3.5 Small（A4B）B300 布局：two-node-mech 做力学检查，four/eight-node 做计时布局。Small 没有单 GPU 训练配方、两节点（8 训练 GPU + 7 引擎 + 1 裁判）是其最小已测配置——见 [configs/miles/examples/README.md:L17-L19](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/examples/README.md#L17-L19)。
458	
459	**练习 2**：示例都写了 `calculate_per_token_loss = true`，为什么库默认仍是 `false`？这两者矛盾吗？
460	
461	**参考答案**：不矛盾。库默认保留 response-mean 是为了兼容既有 run——省略该设置的老配置行为不变；维护示例显式设 `true` 是把新基线写清楚，避免「沉默改变目标」。development-defaults 同样写明「Omitted library settings retain response-mean weighting for compatibility」（Loss weighting 条目，其上一条即本轮新增的 Tiny learning batch and LR）：[docs/miles/development-defaults.md:L18-L23](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/development-defaults.md#L18-L23)。
462	
463	**练习 3**：为什么 README 特意登记「报告的 Small 计时用了 batch 1024 / LR 1e-6 / response-mean」？
464	
465	**参考答案**：因为本轮配方对齐后，当前 Small 基线（256×8、batch 2048、LR 6e-6、token-mean）与历史计时运行的配置不同，且历史运行还未启用 code grading（代码样本未判分、其组被丢弃，每次更新少 3-36 组）——有效工作负载不同。直接沿用旧吞吐数字会误导容量决策，应在新基线下重测。见 [configs/miles/examples/README.md:L21-L25](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/examples/README.md#L21-L25) 与 [docs/miles/olmo35-small.md:L27-L32](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/olmo35-small.md#L27-L32)。

467	## 5. 综合实践
468	
469	**任务：为你的第一次 MILES 冒烟运行制作一页「所有权笔记」，并在 tiny 与 small 两个家族之间做出正确选择。**

471	1. **复制模板**：把 [configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml) 复制到被 git 忽略的 `runs/my-dev.toml`（目录不存在则创建；不要直接改模板——配置约定见 [docs/miles/grpo.md:L42-L49](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/grpo.md#L42-L49)）。
472	2. **改占位符**：替换 `YOUR_USERNAME` 与模型/输出路径（README 的准备步骤见 [configs/miles/examples/README.md:L55-L70](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/examples/README.md#L55-L70)）。
473	3. **无 GPU 规划**：运行 `uv run python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/my-dev.toml`，把输出 JSON 里你认识的段落（model/data/training/inference/core）与 4.2 节架构图逐一连线。
474	4. **家族对照**：并排打开 `tiny/dev.toml` 与 `small/two-node-mech.toml` 的文件头与 `[training]`/`[inference]`/`[miles]` 段，记录三处不同（模型与 checkpoint、拓扑规模、共享的 6e-6/2048/token-mean 基线），并回答：如果只是想验证「MILES 在我的环境能跑通」，该选哪份？如果想测 OLMo 3.5 Small 在 B300 上的吞吐呢？（前者 tiny/dev，后者 small/four-node 或 eight-node，力学检查先用 two-node-mech。）
475	5. **写一页笔记**，回答三个问题：
476	   - 这个 run 里哪些工作由 open-instruct 包装层完成（配置校验、数据准备、GSM8K 验证器、提交回执）？
477	   - 哪些由 MILES 运行时/Core 适配器完成（SGLang rollout、OLMo-core 训练、权重发布、checkpoint）？
478	   - `[core]` 段的 `reward_final_answer_only`/`reward_reasoning_mode`（[configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml:L71-L77](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml#L71-L77)）与 `[miles]` 段的 `calculate_per_token_loss`（[configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml:L84-L87](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml#L84-L87)）最终影响的是哪一层的哪个环节？（提示：判分输入选择见 [docs/miles/grading.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/grading.md)；损失加权语义见 [docs/miles/grpo.md:L88-L107](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/grpo.md#L88-L107)。）

480	
481	预期产物：一张三层架构图 + 一页所有权笔记 + 一份 `plan` 输出的对照标注 + 三行家族对照。`plan` 的具体输出本讲未实际执行，**待本地验证**；若 `plan` 因占位路径报提示，记录提示内容并继续——规划本身不需要那些挂载存在。
482	
483	## 6. 本讲小结
484	
485	- **入口唯一**：`python -m open_instruct.miles` 暴露五个子命令 `plan/validate/train/run/status`（另有 `records` 记录分析）；运行时导入延迟到需要的命令，`plan`/`validate` 无 GPU、无 MILES 运行时即可运行。
486	- **结构化双轨**：含 `schema_version` 或 `model` 的 TOML 编译为 RunSpec（`run`/`status` 只接受这种）；低层 RunConfig 仅供 `plan`/`validate`/`train`。
487	- **三层所有权**：open-instruct 包装层管配置/数据/奖励/提交；MILES 运行时管 rollout 编排与共享 RL 机制；Core 适配器经 OLMo-core 训练、SGLang 服务。后端不导入 open-instruct，open-instruct 以回调与可信注册表注入能力。
488	- **不弃用旧路线**：`grpo.py` 与 `grpo_fast.py` 仍是稠密模型与历史复现的现行选择；MILES 面向受支持的 Olmo MoE 模型。
489	- **文档地图两轮扩展**：上一轮 `grading.md`（共享判分输入）与 `abstention.md`（Nemotron 弃答 QA）；本轮新增 `olmo35-small.md`（B300 实测配方文档，入 mkdocs 导航）、`managed-judges.md` 登记未使用绑定规则、grpo/development-defaults/run-controls/throughput-profiles 的基线措辞翻转为 token-mean。首页表格是精选而非穷举。
490	- **示例家族本轮升级**：`small/dev.toml` 占位被删除，small 家族换成实测 OLMo 3.5 Small B300 三档配方（two-node-mech/four-node/eight-node，配套 moe_configs tile 调优）；全部维护示例统一 token-mean loss，Tiny 学习基线为 256 prompts × 8、batch 2048、恒定 LR 6e-6（详见 u8-l2 与 u8-l15）。
491	
492	## 7. 下一步学习建议
493	
494	下一讲 **u8-l2（配置系统：TOML → RunSpec → RunConfig）** 将拆开本讲只碰了一下的编译链：`configuration/run_spec.py` 的加载与编译、CoreConfig/RunConfig 如何编译出参数列表并挂接奖励/数据钩子、constraints 驱动的校验，以及本轮示例基线翻转（`calculate_per_token_loss=true`）在配置层的含义。
495	
496	在进入下一讲之前，建议先做两件源码阅读：
497	
498	1. 浏览 `open_instruct/miles/configuration/` 目录（`ls` 即可），对照 [docs/miles/architecture.md:L276-L291](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/architecture.md#L276-L291) 的职责表建立印象。
499	2. 通读 [docs/miles/workflow.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/workflow.md)（配合 u8-l3），了解一次 run 从准备、训练到导出的阶段划分，为后续所有 MILES 讲义提供骨架。

# u8-l1 MILES 总览与架构分层

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说出 MILES 与 `grpo.py`（Core/vLLM）、`grpo_fast.py`（DeepSpeed/vLLM）三条 RL 训练路线的关系与各自适用范围。
2. 理解 MILES 的所有权分层：open-instruct 包装层负责什么、MILES 运行时负责什么、Core 适配器经 OLMo-core 与 SGLang 又负责什么。
3. 会用 `python -m open_instruct.miles` 的五个子命令（`plan` / `validate` / `train` / `run` / `status`）以及 `records` 记录分析工具。
4. 知道维护示例按模型家族组织在 `configs/miles/examples/tiny/` 与 `configs/miles/examples/small/` 下：tiny 家族是力学/学习示例，small 家族本轮（PR #2280）从 dev 占位副本升级为实测的 OLMo 3.5 Small（A4B）B300 三档配方（two-node-mech / four-node / eight-node），且全部维护示例的损失基线已翻转为 token-mean（PR #2271）。
5. 了解文档地图的两轮扩展：上一轮新增 `grading.md` 与 `abstention.md`，本轮新增 `olmo35-small.md` 并在 `managed-judges.md` 登记未使用绑定规则。

本讲是 MILES 单元（u8）的第一篇，只做总览不深入细节；配置系统、工作流执行、奖励体系分别在 u8-l2、u8-l3、u8-l6 及之后各讲展开，Small B300 配方的显存账目与吞吐审计另立一讲（u8-l15）。

## 2. 前置知识

阅读本讲前，建议先具备以下概念（不熟悉也没关系，下面用通俗语言解释）：

- **RLVR / GRPO**：可验证奖励强化学习（RL with Verifiable Rewards）。对数学题、代码这类有标准答案的任务，可以用一个「验证器」自动判分作为奖励，而不需要训练额外的奖励模型。GRPO 是一种组相对策略优化算法：对同一个 prompt 采样一组回答，按组内奖励的相对高低计算优势。已在 u6-l1、u6-l2 讲过。
- **rollout（rollout 编排）**：RL 训练的一步是「让当前策略生成一批回答 → 判分 → 用结果更新策略」。生成这批回答的过程及其调度（队列、准入、引擎管理）称为 rollout 编排。
- **Ray actor**：Ray 分布式框架中的常驻进程，持有 GPU 资源并响应远程调用。MILES 运行时用 Ray actor 承载训练器与推理引擎。
- **OLMo-core 与 SGLang**：OLMo-core 是 Allen AI 的模型与分布式训练库（提供模型结构、checkpoint、分布式原语）；SGLang 是推理服务框架。MILES 用前者训练、后者服务。
- **TOML run 文件**：MILES 用一个结构化 TOML 文件描述一次完整运行（模型、数据、拓扑、启动、追踪等），是所有子命令的输入。
- **token-mean 与 response-mean 损失加权**：一个批次里有长有短的回答。response-mean（按响应平均）给每个回答同等权重，长回答里的每个 token 影响被稀释；token-mean（按 token 平均，`calculate_per_token_loss=true`）给每个 token 同等权重。本轮起所有维护示例统一采用 token-mean，但省略该设置时库默认仍是 response-mean，以兼容既有 run。
- **B300 与 MoE**：B300 是 NVIDIA 的 Blackwell Ultra 数据中心 GPU（AI2 的 Holmes 集群使用）；MoE（混合专家）模型每个 token 只激活部分专家参数。OLMo 3.5 Small（A4B）是 256 专家、约 0.8B 激活参数的小型 MoE 模型。
- **Beaker**：AI2 的实验平台，MILES 的 `run` 子命令把 TOML 编译成 Beaker 实验提交。不熟悉 Beaker 也不影响本讲，详见 u8-l8。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| [docs/miles/index.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/index.md) | MILES 文档首页：定位声明、入门顺序、文档地图表、权威性与维护规则 |
| [docs/miles/architecture.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/architecture.md) | 架构与开发：分层所有权表、运行时锁与镜像、启动依赖、本地开发检查、适配器包布局 |
| [open_instruct/miles/__main__.py](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py) | CLI 入口：`python -m open_instruct.miles`，加载 run 文件并分发 plan/validate/train/run/status 与 records |
| [docs/miles/grpo.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/grpo.md) | MILES GRPO 指南：首次运行步骤、配置约定、判分/截断/未判分语义、发布模式 |
| [configs/miles/examples/README.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/examples/README.md) | 维护示例的导读：按模型家族分组（tiny/small），列出六份模板的用途与基线设置 |
| [configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml) | 单 GPU 共置（colocated）微型模型力学检查模板，本讲实践对象 |
| [docs/miles/olmo35-small.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/olmo35-small.md) | 本轮新增（PR #2280）：OLMo 3.5 Small B300 实测布局、显存账目、吞吐审计与失败记录 |
| [configs/miles/moe_configs/README.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/moe_configs/README.md) | 本轮新增：SGLang fused-MoE tile 调优文件的生成、分发与版本匹配规则 |
| [docs/miles/grading.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/grading.md) | 上一轮新增：共享判分输入（ResponseParts、objective/scope/require_response 契约）与行为变更登记 |
| [docs/miles/abstention.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/abstention.md) | 上一轮新增：Nemotron 弃答式 QA 奖励的语义、rubric 与裁判服务复用 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 CLI 入口：`python -m open_instruct.miles`

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

MILES 在 open-instruct 中的公开入口只有一条命令：`python -m open_instruct.miles`。它把「规划、校验、本地执行、Beaker 提交、状态查询」以及「推理记录分析」全部收拢到一个入口后面。

为什么这样设计？

- **研究者的全部意图浓缩在一个 TOML run 文件里**。同一条命令对不同子命令复用同一份配置，避免「训练用一套脚本、提交用另一套脚本」的漂移。
- **运行时导入是延迟的**。GPU/MILES 运行时只在真正需要的子命令里才 import，因此 `plan` / `validate` 这类规划命令在没有 GPU、没有安装 MILES 私有运行时的笔记本电脑上也能运行。这一点是文档明确承诺的：[docs/miles/index.md:L21-L23](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/index.md#L21-L23) 写明 "Planning does not require GPUs or mounted checkpoints"。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

CLI 的一次执行流程：

```text
python -m open_instruct.miles COMMAND CONFIG.toml [--set SECTION.KEY=VALUE ...]
        │
        ├─ sys.argv[1] == "records"？
        │    ├─ "select"        → open_instruct.miles.datasets.record_selection
        │    ├─ "replay-pool"   → open_instruct.miles.datasets.replay_summary
        │    └─ 其他            → miles.utils.record_summary（需 MILES 运行时）
        │
        └─ 否则：argparse 解析 COMMAND ∈ {plan, validate, train, run, status}
             │
             ├─ 读取 TOML → payload
             ├─ 判断结构化：payload 含 schema_version 或 model 字段？
             │    ├─ 是 → specs.from_dict(...) 解析为 RunSpec（结构化 run 文件）
             │    └─ 否 → RunConfig.from_dict(...)（低层原始配置）
             │
             └─ 按命令分发：
                  plan     → config.plan()，打印计划 JSON + 提示（advisories）
                  validate → 结构化：plan() 全量校验；原始：parse_runtime()
                  run      → execution.launch.run()（提交 Beaker，仅限结构化）
                  status   → execution.launch.status()（仅限结构化）
                  train    → workflow.execute(config)（结构化）/ train_config（原始）
                             （OPDRunSpec 走独立的 distillation.opd_runtime 路径）
```

注意两个设计点：

1. **结构化 run 文件与低层配置双轨**。`run`/`status` 只接受 `schema_version=1` 的结构化文件；低层原始配置只支持 `plan`/`validate`/`train`。这让「研究者视角的完整 run」与「底层调参视角的 CoreConfig」都能进门，但提交必须走结构化路线。
2. **错误处理友好**。输入错误（`InputError`）默认被转成一行 `parser.error` 提示而不是一长串 traceback，加 `--debug` 才展开。

### 4.2 架构分层：三层所有权与适配器包布局

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

MILES 不是「又一个训练脚本」，而是把一次 RL 运行拆给三个所有者：

- **open-instruct 包装层**：研究者面对的一切——配置校验、数据准备、验证器/奖励、Beaker 提交与回执、运行产物。
- **MILES 运行时**（私有、按锁定制）：rollout actor、SGLang 推理引擎、采样/优势/损失机制、共享传输。
- **Core 适配器**（位于 MILES 内）：模型构建、打分与训练前向、梯度同步、优化器与 checkpoint、权重导出；训练走 OLMo-core，服务走 SGLang。

为什么要有这条边界？因为 open-instruct 是公开研究仓库，而 MILES 运行时（含其 pinned fork）是独立发布的私有组件。open-instruct 负责「研究者想要什么」，MILES 负责「RL 机制怎么做」，Core 适配器负责「在 OLMo-core 上真正训练」。理解这条边界后，你在 open-instruct 仓库里看到的每个 `open_instruct/miles/` 子包都能归位到某一层。

同时要记住：**MILES 不取代既有 GRPO 训练器**。`grpo.py`（Core/vLLM）与 `grpo_fast.py`（DeepSpeed/vLLM，u6-l4 讲过其 Ray 拓扑）仍是稠密模型训练与历史复现的现行选择；MILES 面向受支持的 Olmo MoE 模型（也提供稠密 Olmo 3 适配器，但验证较少）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

一次 MILES 运行的纵向视角：

```text
研究者编写 run.toml（schema_version=1）
        │  python -m open_instruct.miles plan / validate      ← open-instruct：CPU 校验与规划
        ▼
RunSpec ──编译──▶ RunConfig（含 CoreConfig 与原生 MILES 选项）
        │  python -m open_instruct.miles run                  ← open-instruct：编译 Beaker 实验并提交
        ▼
Beaker 上的应用镜像（按 runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json 构建）
        │
        ▼
MILES 运行时启动：Ray 集群、裁判加载、工作流准备并发启动
        │
        ▼
Core 适配器（OLMoCoreTrainRayActor）：SGLang 服务策略 → rollout → 打分 →
OLMo-core 训练前向/反向 → 权重发布（refresh/barrier/engine_drain）→ checkpoint/导出
```

分层所有权表（五层，前三层是所有权划分，后两层是上游基座）：

| 层 | 拥有 |
|---|---|
| Open Instruct 包装层 | 配置校验、准备、验证器、提交/回执、运行产物 |
| MILES 运行时 | rollout actor、SGLang 引擎、采样/优势/损失机制、共享传输助手 |
| Core 适配器（在 MILES 中） | 模型构建、文档/回放对齐、打分与训练前向、梯度同步、优化器/checkpoint、张量导出 |
| OLMo-core | 模型与分布式训练原语、注意力/专家执行 |
| olmo-sglang | 服务架构注册与模型专属执行 |

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：MILES 与 `grpo_fast.py` 都用 Ray + 多进程做 RL，本质区别是什么？

**参考答案**：`grpo_fast.py` 是 open-instruct 仓库内的一个完整训练脚本（DeepSpeed 训练器 + vLLM 引擎，代码全部在本仓库，u6-l4）；MILES 把「rollout 编排与共享 RL 机制」交给私有 MILES 运行时（按 `runtime.lock.json` 锁定），open-instruct 只保留配置/数据/奖励集成与提交，训练走 OLMo-core、服务走 SGLang。另见 [docs/miles/index.md:L8-L13](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/index.md#L8-L13)：引入 MILES 不弃用既有 GRPO 训练器。

**练习 2**：如果要在 MILES 训练中新增一种自定义验证器，改动应落在哪一层？为什么？

**参考答案**：落在 open-instruct 包装层的 `open_instruct/miles/rewards/`（验证器、奖励路由与托管裁判），以可信注册表条目（factory + 配置）暴露给 MILES。因为后端训练器与托管 rollout 模块不导入 open-instruct（[docs/miles/architecture.md:L304-L313](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/architecture.md#L304-L313)），MILES 侧只通过约定路径消费应用侧回调与注册表。（验证器细节见 u8-l6。）

**练习 3**：为什么 open-instruct 的普通 `uv.lock` 环境跑不了 MILES 训练，而 `plan` 却能跑？

**参考答案**：训练需要 MILES 私有运行时、SGLang 与锁定版本的 OLMo-core，这些由 `runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json` 与专用应用镜像提供（[docs/miles/architecture.md:L25-L30](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/architecture.md#L25-L30)、[docs/miles/architecture.md:L179-L193](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/architecture.md#L179-L193)）；`plan` 只走 CPU 配置代码，CLI 把运行时 import 延迟到需要它的命令（[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L4-L5](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L4-L5)）。

### 4.3 文档地图与两轮扩展

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`docs/miles/` 是 MILES 的权威文档目录：当前指令都住在这里，示例 TOML 表达起始配方，配置代码 + pinned 原生解析器快照 + `runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json` 共同定义「接受哪些设置、运行时来源是什么」。理解文档地图的意义在于：MILES 的文档是**分层且部分自动生成**的——若干参考页由 MkDocs 从配置源在内存中生成、不入库，手写文档与生成文档的维护方式不同。

文档地图近两轮连续扩展，都与本单元后续讲义直接相关：

1. **上一轮新增 `docs/miles/grading.md`（共享判分输入）与 `docs/miles/abstention.md`（Nemotron 弃答 QA）**：grading.md 统一了 MILES 的判分输入——历史上各判分器自己选答案区域，思考里的正确答案可能拿到分而交付答案却是错的；现在由共享的 `ResponseParts` 一次切分 thinking 与交付响应，并用 objective（answer/process/format/composite）× scope × require_response 声明每个验证器的输入契约（深入讲解在 u8-l12）。abstention.md 记录原生弃答式 QA 奖励链路（深入讲解在 u8-l13）。
2. **本轮（28c181666 → 2f7889da9，三个提交）新增 `docs/miles/olmo35-small.md`**（PR #2280）：OLMo 3.5 Small（A4B）B300 的实测布局、显存账目、从 Beaker 工件独立重算的吞吐审计与失败记录，是 `configs/miles/examples/small/` 三档配方的配套文档（深入讲解在 u8-l15）。
3. **本轮的基线措辞翻转**（PR #2271）：`grpo.md` 的 Truncated responses 一节、`development-defaults.md` 的 Loss weighting 条目、`run-controls.md` 与 `throughput-profiles.md` 中的示例数字，全部从 per-response（response-mean）损失改为 token-mean，Tiny 学习示例统一为 256 prompts × 8、batch 2048、恒定 LR 6e-6。
4. **本轮的裁判规则登记**（PR #2286）：`managed-judges.md` 记录「绑定表可以覆盖比所选数据子集更多的源，未使用绑定被允许」（详见 u8-l6/u8-l13）。

### 4.4 示例家族划分：tiny 与 small

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

维护示例（maintained examples）是 MILES 的「配置基线」：除非 run 明确声明，应以示例为准。上一轮（PR #2255）示例按**模型家族**重组为 `tiny/` 与 `small/` 两个目录；本轮（PR #2280/#2271）这两个家族的分工发生实质变化：

- **tiny 家族**：微型模型的力学/学习示例——`dev.toml`（单 GPU 共置力学检查）、`node.toml`（单节点学习）、`three-node.toml`（三节点学习 + 后台评估）。本轮统一了 Tiny 学习基线：256 prompts × 8 responses、batch 2048、恒定 LR 6e-6 无 warmup、token-mean loss。
- **small 家族**：上一轮只是 tiny dev 的副本占位（`small/dev.toml`，为将来的模型/拓扑工作预留）；本轮删除该占位，换成**实测的 OLMo 3.5 Small（A4B，KDA + 256 专家 MoE）B300 三档配方**：`two-node-mech.toml`（两节点力学检查，4 次更新）、`four-node.toml` 与 `eight-node.toml`（计时布局，30 次更新、不存 checkpoint）。

同时，**全部维护示例的损失基线从 per-response 翻转为 token-mean**：`miles.calculate_per_token_loss = true`。注意省略该设置时库默认仍是 `false`（response-mean），这是为兼容既有 run 而刻意保留的——所以每个示例都把它显式写出。

为什么按模型家族分目录？因为 serving 几何、显存账目、准入参数都是模型专属的：Small 文档明确告诫「不要把 Tiny 的 12.5B 推理 preset、评估 profile 或缓存几何复制进 Small」。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

当前六份维护示例的分工（与 README 表格一致）：

| 配置 | 家族 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| `tiny/dev.toml` | tiny | 单 GPU、训练/推理共置；GSM8K 短力学检查 |
| `tiny/node.toml` | tiny | 单个 8 GPU 节点：2 训练 GPU（EP2）+ 6 推理引擎；无裁判 |
| `tiny/three-node.toml` | tiny | 三节点学习：8 训练 GPU（EP8）、15 推理引擎 + 1 裁判；24 GPU，另加后台评估 |
| `small/two-node-mech.toml` | small | OLMo 3.5 Small 力学检查：8 训练 GPU（EP8）、7 引擎、1 裁判；4 次更新 |
| `small/four-node.toml` | small | Small 计时布局：8 训练 GPU（EP8）、23 引擎（R=96）、1 裁判；审计中位数约 302 s/更新 |
| `small/eight-node.toml` | small | Small 计时布局：16 训练 GPU（2 × EP8）、47 引擎（R=96）、1 裁判；晚期窗口中位数约 185 s/更新 |

本轮基线翻转的要点：

```text
损失加权：  per-response（response-mean）      →  token-mean（calculate_per_token_loss = true）
           （省略该设置时库默认仍为 response-mean，兼容既有 run）

Tiny 学习：  128 prompts × 8，batch 1024        →  256 prompts × 8，batch 2048
学习率：    （模板未显式设置）                  →  learning_rate = 6e-6，恒定、无 warmup

small 家族： small/dev.toml（tiny dev 的占位副本）→  three 实测 B300 配方 + docs/miles/olmo35-small.md
                                              +  configs/miles/moe_configs/（fused-MoE tile 调优）
```

一个小陷阱：**历史上的 Small 吞吐计时用的是旧设置**（batch 1024、LR 1e-6、response-mean，且未启用 code grading），与新基线不可直接比较——README 与 olmo35-small.md 都显式登记了这一告诫。

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

**练习 2**：示例都写了 `calculate_per_token_loss = true`，为什么库默认仍是 `false`？这两者矛盾吗？

**练习 3**：为什么 README 特意登记「报告的 Small 计时用了 batch 1024 / LR 1e-6 / response-mean」？

**参考答案**：因为本轮配方对齐后，当前 Small 基线（256×8、batch 2048、LR 6e-6、token-mean）与历史计时运行的配置不同，且历史运行还未启用 code grading（代码样本未判分、其组被丢弃，每次更新少 3-36 组）——有效工作负载不同。直接沿用旧吞吐数字会误导容量决策，应在新基线下重测。见 [configs/miles/examples/README.md:L21-L25](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/configs/miles/examples/README.md#L21-L25) 与 [docs/miles/olmo35-small.md:L27-L32](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/olmo35-small.md#L27-L32)。

## 6. 本讲小结

- **入口唯一**：`python -m open_instruct.miles` 暴露五个子命令 `plan/validate/train/run/status`（另有 `records` 记录分析）；运行时导入延迟到需要的命令，`plan`/`validate` 无 GPU、无 MILES 运行时即可运行。
- **结构化双轨**：含 `schema_version` 或 `model` 的 TOML 编译为 RunSpec（`run`/`status` 只接受这种）；低层 RunConfig 仅供 `plan`/`validate`/`train`。
- **三层所有权**：open-instruct 包装层管配置/数据/奖励/提交；MILES 运行时管 rollout 编排与共享 RL 机制；Core 适配器经 OLMo-core 训练、SGLang 服务。后端不导入 open-instruct，open-instruct 以回调与可信注册表注入能力。
- **不弃用旧路线**：`grpo.py` 与 `grpo_fast.py` 仍是稠密模型与历史复现的现行选择；MILES 面向受支持的 Olmo MoE 模型。
- **文档地图两轮扩展**：上一轮 `grading.md`（共享判分输入）与 `abstention.md`（Nemotron 弃答 QA）；本轮新增 `olmo35-small.md`（B300 实测配方文档，入 mkdocs 导航）、`managed-judges.md` 登记未使用绑定规则、grpo/development-defaults/run-controls/throughput-profiles 的基线措辞翻转为 token-mean。首页表格是精选而非穷举。
- **示例家族本轮升级**：`small/dev.toml` 占位被删除，small 家族换成实测 OLMo 3.5 Small B300 三档配方（two-node-mech/four-node/eight-node，配套 moe_configs tile 调优）；全部维护示例统一 token-mean loss，Tiny 学习基线为 256 prompts × 8、batch 2048、恒定 LR 6e-6（详见 u8-l2 与 u8-l15）。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

下一讲 **u8-l2（配置系统：TOML → RunSpec → RunConfig）** 将拆开本讲只碰了一下的编译链：`configuration/run_spec.py` 的加载与编译、CoreConfig/RunConfig 如何编译出参数列表并挂接奖励/数据钩子、constraints 驱动的校验，以及本轮示例基线翻转（`calculate_per_token_loss=true`）在配置层的含义。

在进入下一讲之前，建议先做两件源码阅读：

1. 浏览 `open_instruct/miles/configuration/` 目录（`ls` 即可），对照 [docs/miles/architecture.md:L276-L291](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/architecture.md#L276-L291) 的职责表建立印象。
2. 通读 [docs/miles/workflow.md](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2f7889da9248629f9415a80a45ba882544b82f1f/docs/miles/workflow.md)（配合 u8-l3），了解一次 run 从准备、训练到导出的阶段划分，为后续所有 MILES 讲义提供骨架。

若想直接深入 Small B300 配方的显存账目、R=96 准入联动与吞吐审计，可跳读 **u8-l15**（依赖 u8-l2 与 u8-l10）；若想横向对比两条 RL 路线的架构差异，可回看 u6-l4（`grpo_fast.py` 的 Ray 拓扑）。

# Environment

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).

- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Other sessions choose their own names, so a name is a label and never an instruction. tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

@@ -297,10 +297,9 @@ These templates inherit the disabled optional startup weight snapshot/reset audi
 audits (`scoring_check_interval = 0`). The first score check at startup/resume, required
 scoring passes, TIS, and publication acknowledgments remain. `dev`
 retains weight qualification. Re-enable audits when changing the publication or
-scoring implementation. Learning templates save every 25 updates; choose the
-cadence from measured save cost and acceptable recovery loss.
+scoring implementation. See the checkpoint policy below before launching a learning run.
 
-All three examples explicitly retain two native checkpoints and disable router
+The examples explicitly retain two native checkpoints and disable router
 auxiliary losses; these differ from the defaults. The learning recipes also keep
 their model-specific context, packing, cache and memory settings. Review these
 choices when changing models. `three-node` keeps its background evaluator configuration
@@ -325,3 +324,41 @@ evaluator does not expose top-p for that external task. Full nucleus-sampling
 alignment requires an evaluator update. Keep benchmark-specific protocols such
 as greedy RULER and BFCL explicit when adding them; do not override every task
 in a suite globally.
+
+## Recovery checkpoints and preserved milestones
+
+The Tiny learning and Small four-/eight-node templates enable native recovery
+saves every **10 updates**, retain the latest **two** saves, and preserve the
+following milestones plus the final checkpoint. Automatic resume is enabled.
+The short mechanics examples keep their separate checkpoint settings.
+
+| Template | Recovery interval | Preserved interval | Reason |
+|---|---:|---:|---|
+| Tiny `node` |10 updates|50 updates|Align native milestones with the existing 50-update development panel.|
+| Tiny `three-node` |10 updates|100 updates|Retain longer learning milestones; its evaluation remains initial/final.|
+| Small `four-node`, `eight-node` |10 updates|50 updates|Retain milestones for expensive runs when extending the 30-update budget.|
+
+Choose the recovery interval from measured **wall-clock update time**, aiming for
+roughly **1–2 hours** between saves. Ten updates is a starting point, not a timer:
+Tiny seed17 data runs at batch 2,048 recently took about 5–7 minutes/update
+(roughly 50–70 minutes per10 updates). This is workload-specific evidence, not a
+throughput claim for every template. The Small timing measurements above used an
+older batch/objective; remeasure the current recipe rather than treating those
+numbers as its checkpoint forecast. Native saves also add I/O time, which the
+historical checkpoint-disabled Small timing runs did not include.
+
+Before launch, budget startup/compilation, generation wait, training, evaluation
+and save time separately. Ensure the **first complete recovery save** should
+finish comfortably inside the protected minimum runtime; if it will not, shorten
+the interval or revise the run budget before submission. Review output storage
+for the latest saves, preserved milestones and evaluator snapshots. For a
+checkpoint-free timing experiment, explicitly disable saving and automatic
+resume and remove `save_interval`; do not carry that override into a learning run.
+
+Verify the first real save's completion manifest, latest pointer and data-cursor
+hash. On interruption, restore the latest complete save and check the first
+post-resume optimizer counter and cursor identity. Check that ordinary saves
+actually roll off while preserved milestones and pending evaluation inputs remain.
+Automatic job restart alone does not establish model/optimizer recovery. See
+[checkpoint retention](../../../docs/miles/models-and-checkpoints.md#save-resume-and-export)
+for native retention semantics.

1	# MILES starting points by model family
2	
3	These templates provide reviewable starting points for MILES training and policy
4	evaluation. Choose a model-family directory, then adapt its paths and topology
5	before launching. The `small` family holds measured OLMo 3.5 Small
6	(A4B) B300 layouts; see [OLMo 3.5 Small on MILES](../../../docs/miles/olmo35-small.md).
7	
8	| Config | Purpose |
9	|---|---|
10	| [tiny/dev.toml](tiny/dev.toml) | One GPU, colocated trainer/inference; short GSM8K mechanics check |
11	| [tiny/node.toml](tiny/node.toml) | One eight-GPU node: 2 trainer GPUs (EP2) and 6 inference engines; no judge |
12	| [tiny/three-node.toml](tiny/three-node.toml) | Three-node learning: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8, one full node), 15 inference engines and 1 judge; 24 GPUs allocated, plus background evaluation |
13	| [small/two-node-mech.toml](small/two-node-mech.toml) | OLMo 3.5 Small mechanics check: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8), 7 engines, 1 judge; 4 updates |
14	| [small/four-node.toml](small/four-node.toml) | Olmo 3.5 Small timing layout: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8), 23 engines (R=96), 1 judge; audited timing4n median ~302 s/update |
15	| [small/eight-node.toml](small/eight-node.toml) | Olmo 3.5 Small timing layout: 16 trainer GPUs (2 × EP8), 47 engines (R=96), 1 judge; audited late-window median ~185 s/update |
16	
17	Use `tiny/dev.toml` for a single-GPU Tiny mechanics check and
18	`small/two-node-mech.toml` for Small mechanics. Small has no single-GPU training
19	recipe; the two-node layout is its smallest tested configuration.
20	
21	All three Small recipes use the Tiny learning baseline from
22	[PR #2271](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/2271): 256 prompts × 8
23	responses, batch 2,048, constant LR 6e-6 with no warmup, and token-mean loss.
24	The reported Small timings used batch 1,024, LR 1e-6 and response-mean loss;
25	see the [Small audit](../../../docs/miles/olmo35-small.md#recipe-alignment).
26	
27	The [generated recipe tables](../../../docs/miles/configuration.md#example-recipes)
28	show current GPU allocations, batch sizes and publication settings directly from
29	these TOMLs. Run `plan` on your copy to inspect the resolved settings and unused GPUs.
30	
31	**The demo configs are the baseline for configuration options unless otherwise
32	stated.** Start a validation run from the applicable demo and record intentional
33	differences. In particular, keep token-mean loss weighting
34	(`miles.calculate_per_token_loss=true`) and zero reward for truncated responses
35	(`core.reward_zero_truncated=true`) and presented-response grading
36	(`core.reward_final_answer_only=true`). The examples declare
37	`core.reward_reasoning_mode="required"`; use `"none"` explicitly for a non-thinking
38	policy/template. Process and boundary-format rewards require declared exceptions;
39	see [grading contracts](../../../docs/miles/grading.md). A throughput experiment must not silently
40	change either learning-policy setting. The one-node and three-node demos share
41	training hyperparameters, including batch size and policy lag; their datasets,
42	judges, evaluation panels and topology-specific performance budgets differ.
43	
44	The examples keep inputs, topology, resource limits and recipe-specific overrides.
45	Launch settings, mounts and input/output paths remain explicit. The examples
46	rely on the structured loader's defaults for optimizer settings, seeds,
47	microbatching, recomputation and dynamic rows. Single-node trainer
48	counts, TP1 inference, one-GPU judges and rubric defaults (2,048 output tokens,
49	temperature 1.0) are omitted where they match the run. Non-default topology and
50	qualification settings remain explicit. See the
51	[complete configuration reference](https://allenai.github.io/open-instruct/miles/configuration/)
52	for options, defaults and interactions, including the linked native-option tables.
53	Use `uv run mkdocs serve` to read the reference for your checkout.
54	
55	## Prepare and launch
56	
57	Copy a starter before editing it:
58	
59	```bash
60	mkdir -p runs
61	cp configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml runs/my-run.toml
62	# Replace model/output paths and YOUR_USERNAME; select an appropriate tiny model.
63	python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/my-run.toml
64	python -m open_instruct.miles validate runs/my-run.toml
65	# Load the pinned binary base into Docker as described in the launch guide.
66	# Build an application image from this clean, committed checkout.
67	unset MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE
68	export MILES_BASE_IMAGE=LOCAL_LOADED_BASE_IMAGE
69	python -m open_instruct.miles run runs/my-run.toml
70	```
71	
72	Do not launch a template unchanged: model, data, output and judge paths are
73	placeholders. Give each run a fresh output directory and keep personal variants
74	in ignored `runs/`.
75	
76	The examples select Holmes for their B300 profiles, high priority and the
77	`ai2/open-instruct-dev` development workspace. These defaults do not imply an
78	available allocation: select a workspace and cluster with capacity before
79	submitting. Keep personal allocation and priority overrides in ignored run files.
80	Review mounts, GPU allocation, minimum runtime and timeout before submission. W&B defaults to offline; set online mode and an API-key secret when
81	needed. See the [launch guide](../../../docs/miles/launching.md).
82	
83	Trainer images are built separately from the TOMLs. Follow the
84	[image build instructions](../../../docs/miles/launching.md#laptop-choose-or-build-an-image)
85	to build the intended application revision and runtime lock. `MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE`
86	can reuse a compatible immutable image; local changes are not overlaid onto it.
87	The launcher checks the image ID, not whether its installed sources match
88	`runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json`. In particular, the cached B300 preset requires
89	the lock's FP32 tracked-state snapshot support; planning cannot detect an older
90	image missing that support. Verify the image's build records against the current
91	lock, or rebuild before submitting.
92	`node` and `three-node` separately pin their evaluator images.
93	
94	## Inputs and expected outputs
95	
96	All three examples explicitly set `data.over_length = "exclude"`, so preparation
97	skips training prompts above the run's effective prompt limit and records
98	original/excluded/retained counts per source in its manifest and logs. Source
99	weights remain unchanged; an emptied configured source or previously populated
100	pool fails preparation, as does an empty overall training input. Reporting-only
101	source groups (`source_dataset`, or `source_name` when absent) may disappear at a
102	smaller budget. Held-out prompts still fail on excess length. The library default
103	remains `"fail"`; remove this example override or set it to `"fail"` to reject
104	over-limit training prompts too.
105	
106	`dev` retains its compatible tiny-checkpoint placeholder and short GSM8K workload.
107	It exercises preparation,
108	generation, training, shared-engine evaluation, native checkpoint saving and final
109	HF export. It is a mechanics check, not an accuracy baseline. A completed run does
110	not test interrupted-run recovery. Filtering is disabled in this example
111	because a tiny model may produce only constant rewards; see
112	[online filtering](../../../docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#online-group-filtering)
113	before changing this for a learning run.
114	
115	`node` adapts the previous two-node `medium` learning recipe to one B300 node,
116	using two EP2 trainer ranks and six TP1 inference engines, with no judge.
117	Its prepared workload contains math, instruction-following and code tasks only;
118	exclude general-quality and other judge-dependent verifiers from training files. The paths use a separate `math-ifeval-code` preparation.
119	Its background GSM8K, GSM8K-Platinum and IFBench panel runs initially, every
120	50 optimizer updates, and finally, using a separate one-GPU allocation. Set
121	`launch.secrets.BEAKER_TOKEN` to enable submission. These starter benchmarks do
122	not cover code quality.
123	This topology passes CPU planning checks; sustained throughput and memory fit
124	still need GPU validation. Supply an HF policy, immutable prepared training
125	JSONL files, and a verifier registry with a code-execution endpoint;
126	the template does not provision a code service.
127	See [datasets and verifiers](../../../docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md) and
128	[managed judges](../../../docs/miles/managed-judges.md).
129	
130	The former topology tier named `small` is retired. For Tiny, use `tiny/dev.toml`
131	for mechanics and `tiny/node.toml` for disaggregated learning. These are distinct
132	from the Olmo 3.5 Small model recipes above. Single-GPU inference alone does not
133	establish that a policy's combined trainer/inference memory footprint fits.
134	
135	`three-node` uses a three-node, 24-GPU footprint. The nodes contain 8 training
136	GPUs, 8 inference GPUs, and 7 inference + 1 judge GPU, respectively; no GPUs
137	are unused.
138	Its starting input is the full published `allenai/Dolci-Think-RL-7B` mixture,
139	including general-quality tasks, prepared according to the
140	[source and preparation contract](../../../docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#three-node-training-mixture).
141	The example's explicit `over_length = "exclude"` keeps the subset that fits the
142	run's prompt budget. This single-file input has no configured source fractions,
143	so exclusions can change source-group proportions. Review the preparation manifest
144	and logs for the retained population; set `over_length = "fail"` when every input
145	row must fit. It requires
146	a prepared Qwen3-32B judge with named verifier bindings. It also requires an
147	accessible `launch.secrets.BEAKER_TOKEN` for background evaluation.
148	Evaluator jobs allocate GPUs beyond the training plan;
149	overlapping jobs can increase that total. Its 25-entry post-training development
150	and text-safety panel runs on the initial/final checkpoints only. With `interval = 0`,
151	periodic evaluation remains disabled even when the run is extended. It preserves pinned task sampling
152	and full evaluation sizes. olmo-eval launches WildGuard/StrongREJECT judges on an extra GPU
153	per safety group. Native SGLang handles policy generation except for SciCode,
154	whose upstream adapter requires the HTTP client. Configure its reference-data path. Code tasks need the sandbox-enabled
155	evaluator image. The full panel still requires GPU/sandbox qualification and
156	measured resource bounds; the starter three-hour evaluator timeout is not a
157	measured full-panel budget.
158	With offline W&B, sync training and manually publish the retained evaluation results.
159	Snapshot cleanup is manual after all referencing jobs stop. See
160	[background evaluation](../../../docs/miles/background-evaluation.md) for the
161	protocol, outputs and limits.

163	For either learning template, check model memory and service capacity before
164	scaling. The [throughput guide](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md) explains
165	how to size memory budgets and engine admission for a model. Follow the
166	[completion checks](../../../docs/miles/operations.md) to verify training,
167	checkpoint and export outputs.
168	
169	## Capacity and qualification settings
170	
171	The three-node throughput candidate uses 256 prompts × 8 samples per collection
172	and one 2,048-sample optimizer batch at constant LR 6e-6 with policy lag 12. It admits
173	3,840 unfinished samples and keeps up to 1,024 completed prompt groups (8,192 samples), and runs 16 HTTP actors per node
174	with one Ray CPU each. The rollout executor reserves two Ray CPUs and each node
175	advertises 64 logical Ray CPUs through `launch.env.OI_MILES_RAY_CPUS` (default
176	32 when omitted). The node example uses the same worker counts and reservations.
177	Both learning examples set `expandable_segments:True` only on trainer ranks.
178	These reservations permit actor placement; they
179	do not make the Python producer event loop parallel. Distributed HTTP actors
180	parse JSON before producer receipt. The single managed Qwen3-32B judge uses CUDA
181	graphs and a maximum of 32 concurrent calls.
182	
183	These are a bundled candidate, not a measured optimum. Increasing the buffer
184	retains more host memory and older work; keep policy lag bounded and watch stale
185	group discards. The one-node validation has a different layout (2 trainers,
186	5 engines and 1 judge) from the judge-free `node.toml` example. It does not
187	qualify three-node throughput. Keep cold compilation, periodic scoring,
188	evaluation and checkpoint cost separate from steady-state measurements.
189	
190	Background evaluation independently sets `evaluation.provider_kwargs.profile` to
191	`"olmo3.5-12.5b"`. It resolves the optimized settings on the assigned evaluator GPU
192	(including H100 80GB and B300), enables full decode graphs, and sizes native
193	harness batches by engine sequence capacity, counting pass@k expansion. SciCode's
194	HTTP server uses the same profile. See the
195	[evaluation guide](../../../docs/miles/background-evaluation.md) for compatibility,
196	batch-boundary limits and full-panel qualification still required.
197	
198	The learning examples pin `inference.profile = "olmo35-b300-12.5@0.8"` on Holmes.
199	This is the current recommended B300 starting point, based on the experiments
200	below. The suffix is **total@active parameters in billions**: approximately
201	12.5B total and 0.8B active per token for the measured model, including embeddings
202	and the output head. The planner recommends one current preset per GPU. The old
203	B300 v1 preset remains only for reproducing older cached configurations.
204	The preset sets **512 running requests, 512 HTTP permits and decode graphs through
205	batch 512 per engine**, 17,825,792 KV tokens, 3,072 recurrent slots, memory fraction
206	0.7 and prefill chunks of 8,192. It disables cross-request radix caching.
207	Both learning examples set `miles.pause_generation_mode = "in_place"`: active
208	requests keep their attention KV and hybrid recurrent state across weight updates,
209	avoiding re-prefill of their generated prefixes. The original `olmo35-b300-v1`
210	preset still enables radix caching with `extra_buffer` and requires retract mode.
211	Runs started from the old examples must resume with their recorded settings;
212	switching profile or pause/cache mode under the same `output.root` fails the
213	recovery configuration check. Use a new root for the updated recipe.
214	The one-GPU colocated `dev.toml` explicitly keeps retract mode; retained state
215	requires dedicated inference GPUs. See the [retained-state qualification](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md#retained-state-weight-publication).
216	Cached hybrid serving requires FP32 tracked-state snapshots in the pinned
217	[runtime](../../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json); rebuild the image when its
218	pins change. See [model limits](../../../docs/miles/moe-model-support.md#current-limits).
219	
220	To move an example to Jupiter, change both the cluster and profile to
221	`olmo35-h100-12.5@0.8`. This preset also uses admission/HTTP/graph batch 512 and prefill
222	chunks of 8,192, but disables caching and uses 6,684,672 KV tokens, 512 recurrent
223	slots and memory fraction 0.9. Both presets require the studied BF16 Olmo 3.5
224	geometry, dedicated TP1 engines and 34,816 context / 32,768 response caps.
225	The old `olmo35-h100-v1` name remains a compatibility alias for the H100 preset.
226	These settings are starting points, not universal memory-fit or throughput guarantees.
227	
228	Named presets apply whole. Any explicit preset-owned key conflicts, even an equal
229	value; errors show the offending keys, an editable TOML block, and two exits:
230	remove the keys to keep the preset, or select `generic` and manage the settings.
231	Known hardware/topology mismatches fail during planning. Model geometry is checked
232	when actual checkpoint metadata is readable and must pass after preparation before
233	training. Preset settings remain identical before and after preparation.
234	
235	Omitted or `generic` profiles preserve generic defaults and explicit settings.
236	The default recurrent pool is 128 slots. A separately measured **cache-off B300
237	alternative uses 1,024 recurrent slots**; it predates the retained-state learning
238	qualification and is an explicit generic-mode experiment, not the current default.
239	Use the named B300 preset for the qualified learning baseline: its 3,072-slot pool
240	was deliberately kept fixed from the prior profile for those runs. SGLang still
241	allocates all explicitly requested slots with radix off; the inherited
242	`extra_buffer` strategy has no effect while radix is disabled. Reducing the pool
243	could save memory but needs separate retained-state qualification before changing
244	the recommendation. A cached-320 H100 alternative uses 4,456,448 KV tokens and 1,920
245	recurrent slots and likewise requires explicit generic settings. Neither alternative
246	is selected automatically. `dev` retains its explicit small colocated configuration.
247	
248	The planner offers read-only tips when a preset matches or explicit pools resemble
249	a preset for different hardware. Tips appear in a stderr box and
250	`plan.runtime.inference_profile.tips`; routine warnings remain plain lines.
251	A cache-off recommendation for retract mode explicitly notes that it disables
252	prefix reuse; compatibility is not a claim of higher throughput for that mode.
253	There is no `auto` selector. Topology, metrics, producer budget and trainer controls
254	remain separate. To experiment, follow
255	[departing from a preset](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md#deliberately-departing-from-a-preset).

259	of the six engines' 3,072 reserved running slots. Filling every reserved slot is
260	useful only when the trainer can consume the resulting work. Compare trainer wait,
261	useful throughput and stale-work discards before increasing the budget.
262	
263	The unfinished-sample budget, when omitted, is
264	`max(collection samples, 2 × engines × min(HTTP permits, running admission))`,
265	rounded to complete prompt groups. The three-node example explicitly uses
266	**3,840** unfinished samples (256 per engine) as a candidate throughput budget. Removing the
267	explicit limits would give 6,144 for node and 15,360 for three-node. Generic
268	64-admission configurations with omitted budgets give
269	1,024 and 1,920 for those topologies. Explicit
270	`async.async_max_concurrent_samples` wins. Completed siblings can remain outside
271	the unfinished budget, so this is not a limit on all retained responses.
272	
273	Both Tiny learning examples use 256 prompts × 8 responses, batch 2,048,
274	constant LR 6e-6 and lag 12.
275	Node buffers one completed batch; three-node buffers four. The three-node
276	unfinished-sample budget represents 1.875 batches;
277	adding the completed buffer gives 5.875 nominal batches. Sample backfill can retain
278	additional finished siblings, so this arithmetic is not an age guarantee. It is headroom, not
279	a measured optimum or a guarantee of steady throughput. Full-recipe
280	collection and judging can limit throughput even with spare engine capacity.

283	reduce the producer budget or fleet when production outruns useful consumption.
284	Per-engine settings do not qualify a whole fleet's routing, refresh latency or
285	learning behavior. See [qualification limits](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md#qualification-limits).

287	The three-node candidate also enables CUDA graphs for its single Qwen3-32B judge
288	and raises judge concurrency from the default 16 to 32. Bounded B300 training
289	runs and H100 TP2 serving checks passed; see the
290	[judge qualification](../../../docs/miles/managed-judges.md#lifecycle-and-audit-artifacts).

292	throughput and the template's policy age. These checks do not establish
293	production-mixture calibration or long-run learning behavior.
294	
295	These templates inherit the disabled optional startup weight snapshot/reset audit
296	(`check_weight_update_equal = false`) and explicitly disable periodic score-reuse
297	audits (`scoring_check_interval = 0`). The first score check at startup/resume, required
298	scoring passes, TIS, and publication acknowledgments remain. `dev`
299	retains weight qualification. Re-enable audits when changing the publication or
300	scoring implementation. See the checkpoint policy below before launching a learning run.
301	
302	The examples explicitly retain two native checkpoints and disable router
303	auxiliary losses; these differ from the defaults. The learning recipes also keep
304	their model-specific context, packing, cache and memory settings. Review these
305	choices when changing models. `three-node` keeps its background evaluator configuration
306	explicit because evaluation changes independently of training topology.
307	
308	`plan` reports copied configurations with no request headroom, forced rescoring,
309	weight qualification, periodic scoring audits, or other diagnostic overhead.
310	Review those warnings instead of inheriting settings from an old experiment.
311	
312	## Candidate evaluation sampling
313	
314	Policy evaluation uses temperature 1.0 and top-p 0.95. Background tasks explicitly
315	request 32,768 response tokens, independent of the serving context size; the math
316	tasks retain 32 draws. Shared in-loop evaluation defaults to the same sampling
317	and caps its inherited response budget at 32K; short smoke tests keep their
318	smaller budgets. Explicit run overrides still win. Judge sampling and training
319	rollout sampling are independent. This candidate protocol awaits the paired
320	control evaluation results.
321	
322	SciCode explicitly sets temperature 1.0 and 32K responses, but the pinned
323	evaluator does not expose top-p for that external task. Full nucleus-sampling
324	alignment requires an evaluator update. Keep benchmark-specific protocols such
325	as greedy RULER and BFCL explicit when adding them; do not override every task
326	in a suite globally.
327	
328	## Recovery checkpoints and preserved milestones
329	
330	The Tiny learning and Small four-/eight-node templates enable native recovery
331	saves every **10 updates**, retain the latest **two** saves, and preserve the
332	following milestones plus the final checkpoint. Automatic resume is enabled.
333	The short mechanics examples keep their separate checkpoint settings.
334	
335	| Template | Recovery interval | Preserved interval | Reason |
336	|---|---:|---:|---|
337	| Tiny `node` |10 updates|50 updates|Align native milestones with the existing 50-update development panel.|
338	| Tiny `three-node` |10 updates|100 updates|Retain longer learning milestones; its evaluation remains initial/final.|
339	| Small `four-node`, `eight-node` |10 updates|50 updates|Retain milestones for expensive runs when extending the 30-update budget.|
340	
341	Choose the recovery interval from measured **wall-clock update time**, aiming for
342	roughly **1–2 hours** between saves. Ten updates is a starting point, not a timer:
343	Tiny seed17 data runs at batch 2,048 recently took about 5–7 minutes/update
344	(roughly 50–70 minutes per10 updates). This is workload-specific evidence, not a
345	throughput claim for every template. The Small timing measurements above used an
346	older batch/objective; remeasure the current recipe rather than treating those
347	numbers as its checkpoint forecast. Native saves also add I/O time, which the
348	historical checkpoint-disabled Small timing runs did not include.
349	
350	Before launch, budget startup/compilation, generation wait, training, evaluation
351	and save time separately. Ensure the **first complete recovery save** should
352	finish comfortably inside the protected minimum runtime; if it will not, shorten
353	the interval or revise the run budget before submission. Review output storage
354	for the latest saves, preserved milestones and evaluator snapshots. For a
355	checkpoint-free timing experiment, explicitly disable saving and automatic
356	resume and remove `save_interval`; do not carry that override into a learning run.
357	
358	Verify the first real save's completion manifest, latest pointer and data-cursor
359	hash. On interruption, restore the latest complete save and check the first
360	post-resume optimizer counter and cursor identity. Check that ordinary saves
361	actually roll off while preserved milestones and pending evaluation inputs remain.
362	Automatic job restart alone does not establish model/optimizer recovery. See
363	[checkpoint retention](../../../docs/miles/models-and-checkpoints.md#save-resume-and-export)
364	for native retention semantics.

# MILES starting points by model family

These templates provide reviewable starting points for MILES training and policy
evaluation. Choose a model-family directory, then adapt its paths and topology
before launching. The `small` family holds measured OLMo 3.5 Small
(A4B) B300 layouts; see [OLMo 3.5 Small on MILES](../../../docs/miles/olmo35-small.md).

| Config | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [tiny/dev.toml](tiny/dev.toml) | One GPU, colocated trainer/inference; short GSM8K mechanics check |
| [tiny/node.toml](tiny/node.toml) | One eight-GPU node: 2 trainer GPUs (EP2) and 6 inference engines; no judge |
| [tiny/three-node.toml](tiny/three-node.toml) | Three-node learning: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8, one full node), 15 inference engines and 1 judge; 24 GPUs allocated, plus background evaluation |
| [small/two-node-mech.toml](small/two-node-mech.toml) | OLMo 3.5 Small mechanics check: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8), 7 engines, 1 judge; 4 updates |
| [small/four-node.toml](small/four-node.toml) | Olmo 3.5 Small timing layout: 8 trainer GPUs (EP8), 23 engines (R=96), 1 judge; audited timing4n median ~302 s/update |
| [small/eight-node.toml](small/eight-node.toml) | Olmo 3.5 Small timing layout: 16 trainer GPUs (2 × EP8), 47 engines (R=96), 1 judge; audited late-window median ~185 s/update |

Use `tiny/dev.toml` for a single-GPU Tiny mechanics check and
`small/two-node-mech.toml` for Small mechanics. Small has no single-GPU training
recipe; the two-node layout is its smallest tested configuration.

All three Small recipes use the Tiny learning baseline from
[PR #2271](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/2271): 256 prompts × 8
responses, batch 2,048, constant LR 6e-6 with no warmup, and token-mean loss.
The reported Small timings used batch 1,024, LR 1e-6 and response-mean loss;
see the [Small audit](../../../docs/miles/olmo35-small.md#recipe-alignment).

The [generated recipe tables](../../../docs/miles/configuration.md#example-recipes)
show current GPU allocations, batch sizes and publication settings directly from
these TOMLs. Run `plan` on your copy to inspect the resolved settings and unused GPUs.

**The demo configs are the baseline for configuration options unless otherwise
stated.** Start a validation run from the applicable demo and record intentional
differences. In particular, keep token-mean loss weighting
(`miles.calculate_per_token_loss=true`) and zero reward for truncated responses
(`core.reward_zero_truncated=true`) and presented-response grading
(`core.reward_final_answer_only=true`). The examples declare
`core.reward_reasoning_mode="required"`; use `"none"` explicitly for a non-thinking
policy/template. Process and boundary-format rewards require declared exceptions;
see [grading contracts](../../../docs/miles/grading.md). A throughput experiment must not silently
change either learning-policy setting. The one-node and three-node demos share
training hyperparameters, including batch size and policy lag; their datasets,
judges, evaluation panels and topology-specific performance budgets differ.

The examples keep inputs, topology, resource limits and recipe-specific overrides.
Launch settings, mounts and input/output paths remain explicit. The examples
rely on the structured loader's defaults for optimizer settings, seeds,
microbatching, recomputation and dynamic rows. Single-node trainer
counts, TP1 inference, one-GPU judges and rubric defaults (2,048 output tokens,
temperature 1.0) are omitted where they match the run. Non-default topology and
qualification settings remain explicit. See the
[complete configuration reference](https://allenai.github.io/open-instruct/miles/configuration/)
for options, defaults and interactions, including the linked native-option tables.
Use `uv run mkdocs serve` to read the reference for your checkout.

## Prepare and launch

Copy a starter before editing it:

```bash
mkdir -p runs
cp configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml runs/my-run.toml
# Replace model/output paths and YOUR_USERNAME; select an appropriate tiny model.
python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/my-run.toml
python -m open_instruct.miles validate runs/my-run.toml
# Load the pinned binary base into Docker as described in the launch guide.
# Build an application image from this clean, committed checkout.
unset MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE
export MILES_BASE_IMAGE=LOCAL_LOADED_BASE_IMAGE
python -m open_instruct.miles run runs/my-run.toml
```

Do not launch a template unchanged: model, data, output and judge paths are
placeholders. Give each run a fresh output directory and keep personal variants
in ignored `runs/`.

The examples select Holmes for their B300 profiles, high priority and the
`ai2/open-instruct-dev` development workspace. These defaults do not imply an
available allocation: select a workspace and cluster with capacity before
submitting. Keep personal allocation and priority overrides in ignored run files.
Review mounts, GPU allocation, minimum runtime and timeout before submission. W&B defaults to offline; set online mode and an API-key secret when
needed. See the [launch guide](../../../docs/miles/launching.md).

Trainer images are built separately from the TOMLs. Follow the
[image build instructions](../../../docs/miles/launching.md#laptop-choose-or-build-an-image)
to build the intended application revision and runtime lock. `MILES_EXISTING_IMAGE`
can reuse a compatible immutable image; local changes are not overlaid onto it.
The launcher checks the image ID, not whether its installed sources match
`runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json`. In particular, the cached B300 preset requires
the lock's FP32 tracked-state snapshot support; planning cannot detect an older
image missing that support. Verify the image's build records against the current
lock, or rebuild before submitting.
`node` and `three-node` separately pin their evaluator images.

skips training prompts above the run's effective prompt limit and records
original/excluded/retained counts per source in its manifest and logs. Source
weights remain unchanged; an emptied configured source or previously populated
pool fails preparation, as does an empty overall training input. Reporting-only
source groups (`source_dataset`, or `source_name` when absent) may disappear at a
smaller budget. Held-out prompts still fail on excess length. The library default
remains `"fail"`; remove this example override or set it to `"fail"` to reject
over-limit training prompts too.

`dev` retains its compatible tiny-checkpoint placeholder and short GSM8K workload.
It exercises preparation,
generation, training, shared-engine evaluation, native checkpoint saving and final

not cover code quality.
This topology passes CPU planning checks; sustained throughput and memory fit
still need GPU validation. Supply an HF policy, immutable prepared training
JSONL files, and a verifier registry with a code-execution endpoint;
the template does not provision a code service.
See [datasets and verifiers](../../../docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md) and
[managed judges](../../../docs/miles/managed-judges.md).
