from the Olmo 3.5 Small model recipes above. Single-GPU inference alone does not
establish that a policy's combined trainer/inference memory footprint fits.

are unused.
Its starting input is the full published `allenai/Dolci-Think-RL-7B` mixture,
including general-quality tasks, prepared according to the
[source and preparation contract](../../../docs/miles/data-and-evaluation.md#three-node-training-mixture).

so exclusions can change source-group proportions. Review the preparation manifest
and logs for the retained population; set `over_length = "fail"` when every input
row must fit. It requires
a prepared Qwen3-32B judge with named verifier bindings. It also requires an
accessible `launch.secrets.BEAKER_TOKEN` for background evaluation.
Evaluator jobs allocate GPUs beyond the training plan;
overlapping jobs can increase that total. Its 25-entry post-training development
and text-safety panel runs on the initial/final checkpoints only. With `interval = 0`,
periodic evaluation remains disabled even when the run is extended. It preserves pinned task sampling
and full evaluation sizes. olmo-eval launches WildGuard/StrongREJECT judges on an extra GPU
per safety group. Native SGLang handles policy generation except for SciCode,
whose upstream adapter requires the HTTP client. Configure its reference-data path. Code tasks need the sandbox-enabled
evaluator image. The full panel still requires GPU/sandbox qualification and
measured resource bounds; the starter three-hour evaluator timeout is not a
measured full-panel budget.
With offline W&B, sync training and manually publish the retained evaluation results.
Snapshot cleanup is manual after all referencing jobs stop. See
[background evaluation](../../../docs/miles/background-evaluation.md) for the
protocol, outputs and limits.

For either learning template, check model memory and service capacity before
scaling. The [throughput guide](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md) explains
how to size memory budgets and engine admission for a model. Follow the
[completion checks](../../../docs/miles/operations.md) to verify training,
checkpoint and export outputs.

below. The suffix is **total@active parameters in billions**: approximately
12.5B total and 0.8B active per token for the measured model, including embeddings
and the output head. The planner recommends one current preset per GPU. The old
B300 v1 preset remains only for reproducing older cached configurations.
The preset sets **512 running requests, 512 HTTP permits and decode graphs through
batch 512 per engine**, 17,825,792 KV tokens, 3,072 recurrent slots, memory fraction
0.7 and prefill chunks of 8,192. It disables cross-request radix caching.
Both learning examples set `miles.pause_generation_mode = "in_place"`: active
requests keep their attention KV and hybrid recurrent state across weight updates,
avoiding re-prefill of their generated prefixes. The original `olmo35-b300-v1`
preset still enables radix caching with `extra_buffer` and requires retract mode.
Runs started from the old examples must resume with their recorded settings;
switching profile or pause/cache mode under the same `output.root` fails the
recovery configuration check. Use a new root for the updated recipe.
The one-GPU colocated `dev.toml` explicitly keeps retract mode; retained state
requires dedicated inference GPUs. See the [retained-state qualification](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md#retained-state-weight-publication).
Cached hybrid serving requires FP32 tracked-state snapshots in the pinned
[runtime](../../../runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json); rebuild the image when its
pins change. See [model limits](../../../docs/miles/moe-model-support.md#current-limits).

To move an example to Jupiter, change both the cluster and profile to
`olmo35-h100-12.5@0.8`. This preset also uses admission/HTTP/graph batch 512 and prefill
chunks of 8,192, but disables caching and uses 6,684,672 KV tokens, 512 recurrent
slots and memory fraction 0.9. Both presets require the studied BF16 Olmo 3.5
geometry, dedicated TP1 engines and 34,816 context / 32,768 response caps.
The old `olmo35-h100-v1` name remains a compatibility alias for the H100 preset.
These settings are starting points, not universal memory-fit or throughput guarantees.

Named presets apply whole. Any explicit preset-owned key conflicts, even an equal
value; errors show the offending keys, an editable TOML block, and two exits:
remove the keys to keep the preset, or select `generic` and manage the settings.
Known hardware/topology mismatches fail during planning. Model geometry is checked
when actual checkpoint metadata is readable and must pass after preparation before
training. Preset settings remain identical before and after preparation.

Omitted or `generic` profiles preserve generic defaults and explicit settings.
The default recurrent pool is 128 slots. A separately measured **cache-off B300
alternative uses 1,024 recurrent slots**; it predates the retained-state learning
qualification and is an explicit generic-mode experiment, not the current default.
Use the named B300 preset for the qualified learning baseline: its 3,072-slot pool
was deliberately kept fixed from the prior profile for those runs. SGLang still
allocates all explicitly requested slots with radix off; the inherited
`extra_buffer` strategy has no effect while radix is disabled. Reducing the pool
could save memory but needs separate retained-state qualification before changing
the recommendation. A cached-320 H100 alternative uses 4,456,448 KV tokens and 1,920
recurrent slots and likewise requires explicit generic settings. Neither alternative
is selected automatically. `dev` retains its explicit small colocated configuration.

The planner offers read-only tips when a preset matches or explicit pools resemble
a preset for different hardware. Tips appear in a stderr box and
`plan.runtime.inference_profile.tips`; routine warnings remain plain lines.
A cache-off recommendation for retract mode explicitly notes that it disables
prefix reuse; compatibility is not a claim of higher throughput for that mode.
There is no `auto` selector. Topology, metrics, producer budget and trainer controls
remain separate. To experiment, follow
[departing from a preset](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md#deliberately-departing-from-a-preset).
Generic mode does not resize pools, estimate memory fit or retain a hardware pin.

The node example explicitly limits unfinished samples to **1,024**, independently
of the six engines' 3,072 reserved running slots. Filling every reserved slot is
useful only when the trainer can consume the resulting work. Compare trainer wait,
useful throughput and stale-work discards before increasing the budget.

The unfinished-sample budget, when omitted, is
`max(collection samples, 2 × engines × min(HTTP permits, running admission))`,
rounded to complete prompt groups. The three-node example explicitly uses
**3,840** unfinished samples (256 per engine) as a candidate throughput budget. Removing the
explicit limits would give 6,144 for node and 15,360 for three-node. Generic
64-admission configurations with omitted budgets give
1,024 and 1,920 for those topologies. Explicit
`async.async_max_concurrent_samples` wins. Completed siblings can remain outside
the unfinished budget, so this is not a limit on all retained responses.

Both Tiny learning examples use 256 prompts × 8 responses, batch 2,048,
constant LR 6e-6 and lag 12.
Node buffers one completed batch; three-node buffers four. The three-node
unfinished-sample budget represents 1.875 batches;
adding the completed buffer gives 5.875 nominal batches. Sample backfill can retain
additional finished siblings, so this arithmetic is not an age guarantee. It is headroom, not
a measured optimum or a guarantee of steady throughput. Full-recipe
collection and judging can limit throughput even with spare engine capacity.
Batch-equivalents do not predict actual policy age or drain duration.
Measure trainer wait, useful throughput, oldest-token age and stale-work discards;
reduce the producer budget or fleet when production outruns useful consumption.
Per-engine settings do not qualify a whole fleet's routing, refresh latency or
learning behavior. See [qualification limits](../../../docs/miles/throughput-profiles.md#qualification-limits).

The three-node candidate also enables CUDA graphs for its single Qwen3-32B judge
and raises judge concurrency from the default 16 to 32. Bounded B300 training
runs and H100 TP2 serving checks passed; see the
[judge qualification](../../../docs/miles/managed-judges.md#lifecycle-and-audit-artifacts).
Continue measuring judge errors and grading latency alongside useful training
throughput and the template's policy age. These checks do not establish
production-mixture calibration or long-run learning behavior.

These templates inherit the disabled optional startup weight snapshot/reset audit
(`check_weight_update_equal = false`) and explicitly disable periodic score-reuse
audits (`scoring_check_interval = 0`). The first score check at startup/resume, required
scoring passes, TIS, and publication acknowledgments remain. `dev`
retains weight qualification. Re-enable audits when changing the publication or
scoring implementation. See the checkpoint policy below before launching a learning run.

The examples explicitly retain two native checkpoints and disable router
auxiliary losses; these differ from the defaults. The learning recipes also keep
their model-specific context, packing, cache and memory settings. Review these
choices when changing models. `three-node` keeps its background evaluator configuration
explicit because evaluation changes independently of training topology.

`plan` reports copied configurations with no request headroom, forced rescoring,
weight qualification, periodic scoring audits, or other diagnostic overhead.
Review those warnings instead of inheriting settings from an old experiment.

## Candidate evaluation sampling

Policy evaluation uses temperature 1.0 and top-p 0.95. Background tasks explicitly
request 32,768 response tokens, independent of the serving context size; the math
tasks retain 32 draws. Shared in-loop evaluation defaults to the same sampling
and caps its inherited response budget at 32K; short smoke tests keep their
smaller budgets. Explicit run overrides still win. Judge sampling and training
rollout sampling are independent. This candidate protocol awaits the paired
control evaluation results.

SciCode explicitly sets temperature 1.0 and 32K responses, but the pinned
evaluator does not expose top-p for that external task. Full nucleus-sampling
alignment requires an evaluator update. Keep benchmark-specific protocols such
as greedy RULER and BFCL explicit when adding them; do not override every task
in a suite globally.

## Recovery checkpoints and preserved milestones

The Tiny learning and Small four-/eight-node templates enable native recovery
saves every **10 updates**, retain the latest **two** saves, and preserve the
following milestones plus the final checkpoint. Automatic resume is enabled.
The short mechanics examples keep their separate checkpoint settings.

| Template | Recovery interval | Preserved interval | Reason |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Tiny `node` |10 updates|50 updates|Align native milestones with the existing 50-update development panel.|
| Tiny `three-node` |10 updates|100 updates|Retain longer learning milestones; its evaluation remains initial/final.|
| Small `four-node`, `eight-node` |10 updates|50 updates|Retain milestones for expensive runs when extending the 30-update budget.|

Choose the recovery interval from measured **wall-clock update time**, aiming for
roughly **1–2 hours** between saves. Ten updates is a starting point, not a timer:
Tiny seed17 data runs at batch 2,048 recently took about 5–7 minutes/update
(roughly 50–70 minutes per10 updates). This is workload-specific evidence, not a
throughput claim for every template. The Small timing measurements above used an
older batch/objective; remeasure the current recipe rather than treating those
numbers as its checkpoint forecast. Native saves also add I/O time, which the
historical checkpoint-disabled Small timing runs did not include.

Before launch, budget startup/compilation, generation wait, training, evaluation
and save time separately. Ensure the **first complete recovery save** should
finish comfortably inside the protected minimum runtime; if it will not, shorten
the interval or revise the run budget before submission. Review output storage
for the latest saves, preserved milestones and evaluator snapshots. For a
checkpoint-free timing experiment, explicitly disable saving and automatic
resume and remove `save_interval`; do not carry that override into a learning run.

Verify the first real save's completion manifest, latest pointer and data-cursor
hash. On interruption, restore the latest complete save and check the first
post-resume optimizer counter and cursor identity. Check that ordinary saves
actually roll off while preserved milestones and pending evaluation inputs remain.
Automatic job restart alone does not establish model/optimizer recovery. See
[checkpoint retention](../../../docs/miles/models-and-checkpoints.md#save-resume-and-export)
for native retention semantics.

1	# OLMo 3.5 Small (A4B) on B300
2	
3	Measured MILES RL layouts for OLMo 3.5 Small ("Hero Small", A4B,
4	`olmo35-small-e256k8-sh2x`) on `ai2/holmes` B300 nodes. Configs:
5	[two-node-mech](../../configs/miles/examples/small/two-node-mech.toml),
6	[four-node](../../configs/miles/examples/small/four-node.toml) and
7	[eight-node](../../configs/miles/examples/small/eight-node.toml). The current recipes
8	use the Tiny batch/LR/loss baseline from PR #2271; historical measurements below
9	used the earlier settings. They run four mechanics or 30 timing updates without
10	checkpoints and do not establish learning quality.
11	
12	## Model and start checkpoint
13	
14	- Start checkpoint: H203 SFT export
15	  `/weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/abhishekr/a4b-gpu/a4bgpu-s34521/hf_step18410`
16	  (`Olmo3MoeForCausalLM`, bf16, 72.58B parameters / 145.16 GB).
17	- 40 layers: 35 KDA plus full attention at layers 7, 15, 23, 31 and 39 (NoPE, head_dim 256);
18	  256 routed experts top-8 (latent MoE dim 768, `moe_intermediate_size` 3072), shared expert,
19	  dense layer 0; hidden 1536; untied LM head.
20	- Export notes: the `emo_*` fields are all null in this SFT export (the base export has
21	  EMo 8/256/256), so it is used as-is with no config edit. The HF config has
22	  `vocab_size` 100278 (LM head `[100278, 1536]`); 100352 is Core's padded size.
23	- Data: robertb's H196 Dolci inputs
24	  (`/weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/robertb/miles/h196-dolci-control-20261113/inputs/`,
25	  84,577 rendered rows). Its rendering was made for Tiny but uses the same tokenizer and chat
26	  template as this export. There is no held-out split, so do not set `training.eval_interval`.
27	- Code verifier needs `CODE_EXECUTION_TOKEN`. Each recipe maps it to a placeholder
28	  Beaker secret name under `[launch.secrets]`; replace that name with a secret in the
29	  selected workspace. Never put the token value in the TOML. The historical timing
30	  runs omitted this credential: code samples were ungraded and their groups dropped
31	  (3-36 groups per update). Runs with code grading enabled have a different effective
32	  workload; remeasure throughput rather than assuming the historical timings apply.
33	
34	## Layout and memory
35	
36	| Config | Nodes | Trainer | Engines | Judge |
37	|---|---|---|---|---|
38	| two-node-mech | 2 | 8 GPUs, EP8 | 7 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |
39	| four-node | 4 | 8 GPUs, EP8 | 23 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |
40	| eight-node | 8 | 16 GPUs, 2 nodes × EP8 | 47 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |
41	
42	- Trainer (EP8, 4 nodes): peak reserved 220.5 GiB of 268.6 GiB per B300 (rank 0 peak
43	  allocated 209.7 GiB). With 2 × EP8 (8 nodes): 169.7 GiB. Packs are 34,816 tokens, below the
44	  OLMo-core no-grad Triton SwiGLU int32 overflow at 43,690 tokens per forward.
45	- Engine at R=96: weights 135 GB; KDA state for 128 slots 17.9 GB (SSM 17.64 + conv 0.21);
46	  KV for 3,342,336 tokens 63.8 GB (K 31.88 + V 31.88); about 50 GB free after pools at
47	  `mem_fraction_static` 0.88.
48	
49	## Settings that matter
50	
51	- `sglang_attention_backend = "trtllm_mha"` for the 5 full-attention layers. On one engine with
52	  96 forced 4K decodes: 2,881 tok/s vs 2,473 with triton. `fa4` crashes the server: "SM100
53	  forward with head_dim=256 does not support seqused_q/seqused_k".
54	- Tuned fused-MoE tiles (`SGLANG_MOE_CONFIG_DIR`, see
55	  [moe_configs](../../configs/miles/moe_configs/README.md)): kernel -9% at batch 96, decode
56	  +1.6% at R=96. The tiles only take effect in an image built with this branch's
57	  `configs/miles`; an older image has no file at that path.
58	- `OLMO_SGLANG_CORE_COMPAT = "rounding"`. The attention trial's HF vs SGLang
59	  samples have mean |Δlogprob| 0.0155-0.0223 and argmax agreement 98.2-99.4%.
60	- Admission R=96: `sglang_max_running_requests` 96, `sglang_max_mamba_cache_size` 128,
61	  `sglang_server_concurrency` 192, `sglang_cuda_graph_max_bs_decode` 96, producer budget
62	  `async_max_concurrent_samples` = 96 × engines.
63	- Judge: `timeout = 600` and `chat_template = "qwen3-no-thinking"`. The judge bindings use the
64	  hashed verifier ids in the H196 `verifiers.json`.
65	- `two-node-mech` enables the initial serving-weight comparison and repeats the
66	  standalone/training scoring check every update. These qualification checks add
67	  overhead relative to the original mechanics run and remain off in timing recipes
68	  (which retain the default startup scoring check).
69	- The four/eight-node recipes request 4h/3h of protected runtime, respectively,
70	  based on historical startup and update times plus headroom, with an 8h timeout.
71	  Revisit these budgets when enabling code grading or other additional work.
72	
73	## Results
74	
75	The table below was independently recomputed from retained Beaker artifacts on
76	November 18, 2026. Updates 10-29 unless noted, 128 prompts × 8 samples, max response
77	32,768 tokens. A cycle starts at `generation_wait.started_unix` and ends at
78	`publication.started_unix + publication.seconds` for the same update. Startup,
79	final drain and checkpoint/evaluation work are excluded. Each column is its own
80	median; component medians need not sum to the cycle median. Earlier headline cycle
81	figures (299/309/399/139 seconds) were not reproduced by this definition.
82	
83	| Run | Layout | s/update (wall median) | Gen wait | Train | Publication | Engine tok/s | Notes |
84	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
85	| [timing4](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7EWK861JCP5Z0G5514S5XJ5) | 4-node, R=96 | 276.2 (u10-24) | 109.6 | 171.2 | 8.9 | 2,528 | Failed at update 25: `/weka/oe-training-default` full |
86	| [timing4n](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7HF4C8M7XC7ZPVC9QMD8X36) | 4-node, R=96 | 301.7 | 125.7 | 174.7 | 9.1 | 2,524 | 30/30, clean exit |
87	| [timing4n-r64](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7J0V7M8VHN4X1PJ43BQ9JZQ) | 4-node, R=64 | 396.4 | 217.5 | 163.8 | 7.2 | 1,946 | 31% slower cycle median than R=96 |
88	| [timing8](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7FV0QBE1CJ2656N5DA0JYY6), u10-23 | 8-node, R=96 | 116.0 | 0.3 | 98.1 | 17.7 | 2,371 | Drains buffered work; not a steady-state topology result |
89	| timing8, u24-29 | 8-node, R=96 | 185.5 | 73.8 | 96.0 | 18.3 | — | Only six late updates; shutdown subsequently failed |
90	| [timing4n-r160](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7NHRMV28ZX4S3HXD4BWAQVJ), u10-29 | 4-node, R=160 | 182.7 | 0.3 | 163.8 | 10.0 | — | Early buffered work; 50 updates total |
91	| timing4n-r160, u30-49 | 4-node, R=160 | 248.9 | 64.8 | 173.3 | 9.8 | — | Later window; shutdown subsequently failed |
92	
93	The engine token rates above retain the original serving summaries; cycle and stage
94	durations were audited directly. `driver_timing.jsonl`, `rollout_flow.jsonl`,
95	`pipeline_occupancy.jsonl`, `publication.jsonl`, all-rank `training_contract_rank*.jsonl`
96	and actor metric events are in each experiment's `run/checkpoints/` results.
97	The R96 and R64 runs pass `scripts/miles/analyze_throughput.py` with `warmup=10`,
98	including all eight trainer ranks and completed workflow checks. All 16 timing8
99	ranks and all eight R160 ranks completed their requested 30/50 optimizer steps,
100	respectively, without skipped updates; those experiments still failed at shutdown.
101	
102	### Topology interpretation
103	
104	- Four-node R96: trainer rollout-wait share is **35.5%** of measured driver-stage
105	  time over u10-29. R64 increases it to **54.2%**. The R96 trial delivers about
106	  30.6K useful response tokens/s versus 22.4K for R64, a 37% improvement under the
107	  strict analyzer. Publication is about 9 seconds/update and is not the largest cost.
108	- Eight-node R96: early compilation and slow trainer updates build a generation
109	  backlog. Median completed queue depth falls from 384 groups over u10-23 to zero
110	  over u24-29. Late trainer wait is **36.5%**; doubling both trainer and inference
111	  capacity did not eliminate rollout starvation. Late stale-token discard fraction
112	  is **9.3%** of delivered plus stale-discarded response tokens. Mean sample policy
113	  age has a per-update median of 8.0 versions in u10-23 and 4.9 in u24-29, versus
114	  2.2 for four-node R96. These are different operating regimes.
115	- Four-node R160: the later u30-49 window reduces wait to **24.9%**, with median
116	  sample age 3.3 versions and no stale-token discards in that window. Its early
117	  near-zero wait is not a steady-state result. This is a promising next candidate,
118	  not a qualified replacement: it failed the same final-drain boundary and has not
119	  been repeated with code grading or newer batch/loss settings.
120	- HTTP permit wait and generation-admission wait are zero at the median in these
121	  windows; unfinished work is near its configured budget. This does not isolate
122	  the judge's contribution. Rollout wait includes production, filtering and grading,
123	  and cannot be attributed entirely to policy GPU inference without more evidence.
124	- Even the successful four-node R96 run drains for 741 seconds at shutdown and
125	  leaves 29.4M completed response tokens unused (10.5% of accounted delivered plus
126	  stale-discarded plus terminal-unused tokens). Warm-cycle throughput is not a
127	  complete job-cost metric.
128	
129	The optimization evidence supports the attention backend, tuned tiles and increasing
130	admission above 64. It does not establish an optimal trainer/engine split. Compare
131	longer runs with the same workload and objective, useful tokens per allocated GPU-hour,
132	policy age, stale/unused work and judge time before selecting a production topology.
133	
134	### Recipe alignment
135	
136	All three Small recipes, including mechanics, now use the Tiny learning baseline
137	from [PR #2271](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/2271):
138	
139	| Setting | Current Small baseline | Historical Small measurements |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| Prompts × responses per prompt | 256 × 8 | 128 × 8 |
142	| Responses per optimizer update | 2,048 | 1,024 |
143	| Learning rate | 6e-6, constant, no warmup | 1e-6, constant, no warmup |
144	| Loss weighting | Token mean | Response mean |
145	| Group-standard-deviation normalization | Off | Off |
146	
147	This is the starting baseline for Small; the historical throughput results do not
148	measure this combination. The serving geometry remains the submitted timing4n/timing8
149	geometry. Paths, credentials, runtime budgets and mechanics qualification controls
150	also have the documented changes above.
151	
152	The completed-buffer factor stays four: 1,024 prompt groups / 8,192 responses.
153	Unfinished producer budgets remain 672, 2,208 and 4,512 for the two/four/eight-node
154	layouts, respectively (0.328, 1.078 and 2.203 optimizer batches). The nominal sum
155	of unfinished budget plus completed-buffer capacity is therefore 4.328, 5.078 and
156	6.203 batches. Finished siblings can live outside that accounting; these figures
157	are not policy-age guarantees. Inspect measured age and useful throughput when
158	tuning the new baseline.
159	Do not copy Tiny's 12.5B inference preset, evaluator profile or cache geometry into
160	Small: those are model-specific. Checkpoint/export/evaluation differences here are
161	intentional for disposable timing runs, not a learning-run baseline.
162	
163	- Trainer: ~6.9K tok/s/GPU at EP8 on 4 nodes; ~6.0K tok/s/GPU with 2 × EP8; about 8.6-8.9M
164	  model tokens per update.
165	- Response lengths are long: the median of per-update mean accepted lengths is about 8.1-8.4K
166	  tokens, truncation is 0-6%, and about 25% of groups are zero-std.
167	- Startup to the end of update 0: 1,953-2,429 s on 4 nodes, 1,543 s on 8 nodes.
168	- timing8 completed all 30 updates, then exited 1 at teardown because the final generation drain
169	  hit its 900 s timeout. Terminal refresh cleanup now cancels unused generation through
170	  the existing backend shutdown API before closing weight transport and disposing
171	  servers. This change has CPU runtime regression coverage; a clean Small GPU run
172	  is still required. Evaluation and final HF export retain their generation-drain
173	  boundaries because they may reuse live serving resources.
174	
175	## What did not work or was not tested
176	
177	- `fa4` attention: crashes on head_dim 256 (above).
178	- R=64: slower (396 vs 302 s/update); engines gain throughput up to R=96. In single-engine
179	  forced decodes, R=144 matched R=96 and R=192 gave +19% total tok/s with each request ~40%
180	  slower.
181	- EP4 trainer: untested.
182	
183	## Code and runtime
184	
185	The original timing runs needed no Small-specific adapter or weight-sync changes. timing4 ran on image
186	01M7A0QM57N9499PGFAT73SMF0 (open-instruct a87a0feac). timing4n and r64 ran on image
187	01M7GA94Q6GKMP2MV2N36YE83Q, built from open-instruct 5c6645da. That is main 28c18166 plus an
188	SGLang pin with an Olmo 3 sliding-window KV backport, which Small (no sliding-window layers)
189	does not use. `plan` on main resolves the timing4n config identically to 5c6645da. These
190	examples have not been run on an image built from main.
191	
192	## Qualification before a learning run
193	
194	Copy `two-node-mech.toml` to ignored `runs/`, set a fresh output path and the actual
195	workspace/secret names, then inspect `python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/small-mech.toml`
196	and `python -m open_instruct.miles validate runs/small-mech.toml` before using the
197	[committed-image launcher](launching.md). Build the image from the revision being
198	qualified; `plan` equality cannot establish runtime equality.
199	
200	Retain the Beaker experiment link, image ID, submitted TOML and completion artifacts.
201	Verify all four updates, successful code grading, passing initial weight comparison,
202	standalone/training score agreement, publication acknowledgments and a clean exit.
203	Inspect `refresh_scores` for mixed-version responses and their historical-prefix and
204	latest-forward log-ratio diagnostics; see [Core diagnostics](core.md) and
205	[mixed-policy refresh](async-pipeline.md#mixed-policy-refresh). Those ratios include
206	policy drift and are not an isolated numerical-parity measurement.
207	
208	For publication debugging, enable `core.diagnostic_interval = 1` with
209	`miles.check_weight_update_equal = true` in the run copy to exercise the existing
210	snapshot/reset/republish checks after optimizer updates. This adds a second transfer
211	and extra gradient/update diagnostics. The check detects incomplete transfers over
212	its selected tensors; it does not independently prove the export mapping. Keep a
213	separate Core-versus-serving score comparison on identical tokens, prefixes and
214	weights as a qualification requirement. HF-versus-SGLang greedy agreement and an
215	always-zero training metric do not establish that comparison.
216	
217	Longer learning runs additionally need native checkpoint/save-resume and evaluation
218	checks. The historical timing runs disabled saving; the current four-/eight-node starters
219	enable bounded recovery saves. Their inputs still have no held-out split.
220	
221	## Open items
222	
223	- R160 finished 50 updates, then failed its 900-second final generation drain.
224	  It used server concurrency 320, 192 KDA slots, CUDA graph batch 160, producer
225	  budget 3,680 and an auto-sized KV pool. Repeat after the terminal-cleanup fix
226	  and under the intended code-grading and batch/loss configuration.
227	- Judge latency is not logged per call, so the judge's share of generation wait is unmeasured.
228	- The earlier claim that `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` is always zero was incorrect.
229	  Raw actor metric events record about 0.008 over the measured timing windows;
230	  `collection_score_mean_abs` is about 0.0065-0.0067. These combine numerical and
231	  policy differences; they do not replace a controlled same-weight parity check.
232	
233	## Checkpoint settings in the current starters
234	
235	The four- and eight-node templates now enable 10-update native recovery saves,
236	automatic resume, retention of the latest two saves and 50-update permanent
237	milestones, plus a final native save. Their 30-update starting budgets therefore
238	save at 10/20/30; 50-update retention becomes relevant when the run is extended.
239	The four-update two-node mechanics check still disables checkpoints/resume.

# OLMo 3.5 Small (A4B) on B300

Measured MILES RL layouts for OLMo 3.5 Small ("Hero Small", A4B,
`olmo35-small-e256k8-sh2x`) on `ai2/holmes` B300 nodes. Configs:
[two-node-mech](../../configs/miles/examples/small/two-node-mech.toml),
[four-node](../../configs/miles/examples/small/four-node.toml) and
[eight-node](../../configs/miles/examples/small/eight-node.toml). The current recipes
use the Tiny batch/LR/loss baseline from PR #2271; historical measurements below
used the earlier settings. They run four mechanics or 30 timing updates without
checkpoints and do not establish learning quality.

## Model and start checkpoint

- Start checkpoint: H203 SFT export
  `/weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/abhishekr/a4b-gpu/a4bgpu-s34521/hf_step18410`
  (`Olmo3MoeForCausalLM`, bf16, 72.58B parameters / 145.16 GB).
- 40 layers: 35 KDA plus full attention at layers 7, 15, 23, 31 and 39 (NoPE, head_dim 256);
  256 routed experts top-8 (latent MoE dim 768, `moe_intermediate_size` 3072), shared expert,
  dense layer 0; hidden 1536; untied LM head.
- Export notes: the `emo_*` fields are all null in this SFT export (the base export has
  EMo 8/256/256), so it is used as-is with no config edit. The HF config has
  `vocab_size` 100278 (LM head `[100278, 1536]`); 100352 is Core's padded size.
- Data: robertb's H196 Dolci inputs
  (`/weka/olmo-3p5-post-checkpoints/robertb/miles/h196-dolci-control-20261113/inputs/`,
  84,577 rendered rows). Its rendering was made for Tiny but uses the same tokenizer and chat
  template as this export. There is no held-out split, so do not set `training.eval_interval`.
- Code verifier needs `CODE_EXECUTION_TOKEN`. Each recipe maps it to a placeholder
  Beaker secret name under `[launch.secrets]`; replace that name with a secret in the
  selected workspace. Never put the token value in the TOML. The historical timing
  runs omitted this credential: code samples were ungraded and their groups dropped
  (3-36 groups per update). Runs with code grading enabled have a different effective
  workload; remeasure throughput rather than assuming the historical timings apply.

## Layout and memory

| Config | Nodes | Trainer | Engines | Judge |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| two-node-mech | 2 | 8 GPUs, EP8 | 7 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |
| four-node | 4 | 8 GPUs, EP8 | 23 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |
| eight-node | 8 | 16 GPUs, 2 nodes × EP8 | 47 × TP1 | 1 × Qwen3-32B |

- Trainer (EP8, 4 nodes): peak reserved 220.5 GiB of 268.6 GiB per B300 (rank 0 peak
  allocated 209.7 GiB). With 2 × EP8 (8 nodes): 169.7 GiB. Packs are 34,816 tokens, below the
  OLMo-core no-grad Triton SwiGLU int32 overflow at 43,690 tokens per forward.
- Engine at R=96: weights 135 GB; KDA state for 128 slots 17.9 GB (SSM 17.64 + conv 0.21);
  KV for 3,342,336 tokens 63.8 GB (K 31.88 + V 31.88); about 50 GB free after pools at
  `mem_fraction_static` 0.88.

## Settings that matter

- `sglang_attention_backend = "trtllm_mha"` for the 5 full-attention layers. On one engine with
  96 forced 4K decodes: 2,881 tok/s vs 2,473 with triton. `fa4` crashes the server: "SM100
  forward with head_dim=256 does not support seqused_q/seqused_k".
- Tuned fused-MoE tiles (`SGLANG_MOE_CONFIG_DIR`, see
  [moe_configs](../../configs/miles/moe_configs/README.md)): kernel -9% at batch 96, decode
  +1.6% at R=96. The tiles only take effect in an image built with this branch's
  `configs/miles`; an older image has no file at that path.
- `OLMO_SGLANG_CORE_COMPAT = "rounding"`. The attention trial's HF vs SGLang
  samples have mean |Δlogprob| 0.0155-0.0223 and argmax agreement 98.2-99.4%.
- Admission R=96: `sglang_max_running_requests` 96, `sglang_max_mamba_cache_size` 128,
  `sglang_server_concurrency` 192, `sglang_cuda_graph_max_bs_decode` 96, producer budget
  `async_max_concurrent_samples` = 96 × engines.
- Judge: `timeout = 600` and `chat_template = "qwen3-no-thinking"`. The judge bindings use the
  hashed verifier ids in the H196 `verifiers.json`.
- `two-node-mech` enables the initial serving-weight comparison and repeats the
  standalone/training scoring check every update. These qualification checks add
  overhead relative to the original mechanics run and remain off in timing recipes
  (which retain the default startup scoring check).
- The four/eight-node recipes request 4h/3h of protected runtime, respectively,
  based on historical startup and update times plus headroom, with an 8h timeout.
  Revisit these budgets when enabling code grading or other additional work.

## Results

The table below was independently recomputed from retained Beaker artifacts on
November 18, 2026. Updates 10-29 unless noted, 128 prompts × 8 samples, max response
32,768 tokens. A cycle starts at `generation_wait.started_unix` and ends at
`publication.started_unix + publication.seconds` for the same update. Startup,
final drain and checkpoint/evaluation work are excluded. Each column is its own
median; component medians need not sum to the cycle median. Earlier headline cycle
figures (299/309/399/139 seconds) were not reproduced by this definition.

| Run | Layout | s/update (wall median) | Gen wait | Train | Publication | Engine tok/s | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [timing4](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7EWK861JCP5Z0G5514S5XJ5) | 4-node, R=96 | 276.2 (u10-24) | 109.6 | 171.2 | 8.9 | 2,528 | Failed at update 25: `/weka/oe-training-default` full |
| [timing4n](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7HF4C8M7XC7ZPVC9QMD8X36) | 4-node, R=96 | 301.7 | 125.7 | 174.7 | 9.1 | 2,524 | 30/30, clean exit |
| [timing4n-r64](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7J0V7M8VHN4X1PJ43BQ9JZQ) | 4-node, R=64 | 396.4 | 217.5 | 163.8 | 7.2 | 1,946 | 31% slower cycle median than R=96 |
| [timing8](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7FV0QBE1CJ2656N5DA0JYY6), u10-23 | 8-node, R=96 | 116.0 | 0.3 | 98.1 | 17.7 | 2,371 | Drains buffered work; not a steady-state topology result |
| timing8, u24-29 | 8-node, R=96 | 185.5 | 73.8 | 96.0 | 18.3 | — | Only six late updates; shutdown subsequently failed |
| [timing4n-r160](https://beaker.org/ex/01M7NHRMV28ZX4S3HXD4BWAQVJ), u10-29 | 4-node, R=160 | 182.7 | 0.3 | 163.8 | 10.0 | — | Early buffered work; 50 updates total |
| timing4n-r160, u30-49 | 4-node, R=160 | 248.9 | 64.8 | 173.3 | 9.8 | — | Later window; shutdown subsequently failed |

The engine token rates above retain the original serving summaries; cycle and stage
durations were audited directly. `driver_timing.jsonl`, `rollout_flow.jsonl`,
`pipeline_occupancy.jsonl`, `publication.jsonl`, all-rank `training_contract_rank*.jsonl`
and actor metric events are in each experiment's `run/checkpoints/` results.
The R96 and R64 runs pass `scripts/miles/analyze_throughput.py` with `warmup=10`,
including all eight trainer ranks and completed workflow checks. All 16 timing8
ranks and all eight R160 ranks completed their requested 30/50 optimizer steps,
respectively, without skipped updates; those experiments still failed at shutdown.

### Topology interpretation

- Four-node R96: trainer rollout-wait share is **35.5%** of measured driver-stage
  time over u10-29. R64 increases it to **54.2%**. The R96 trial delivers about
  30.6K useful response tokens/s versus 22.4K for R64, a 37% improvement under the
  strict analyzer. Publication is about 9 seconds/update and is not the largest cost.
- Eight-node R96: early compilation and slow trainer updates build a generation
  backlog. Median completed queue depth falls from 384 groups over u10-23 to zero
  over u24-29. Late trainer wait is **36.5%**; doubling both trainer and inference
  capacity did not eliminate rollout starvation. Late stale-token discard fraction
  is **9.3%** of delivered plus stale-discarded response tokens. Mean sample policy
  age has a per-update median of 8.0 versions in u10-23 and 4.9 in u24-29, versus
  2.2 for four-node R96. These are different operating regimes.
- Four-node R160: the later u30-49 window reduces wait to **24.9%**, with median
  sample age 3.3 versions and no stale-token discards in that window. Its early
  near-zero wait is not a steady-state result. This is a promising next candidate,
  not a qualified replacement: it failed the same final-drain boundary and has not
  been repeated with code grading or newer batch/loss settings.
- HTTP permit wait and generation-admission wait are zero at the median in these
  windows; unfinished work is near its configured budget. This does not isolate
  the judge's contribution. Rollout wait includes production, filtering and grading,
  and cannot be attributed entirely to policy GPU inference without more evidence.
- Even the successful four-node R96 run drains for 741 seconds at shutdown and
  leaves 29.4M completed response tokens unused (10.5% of accounted delivered plus
  stale-discarded plus terminal-unused tokens). Warm-cycle throughput is not a
  complete job-cost metric.

The optimization evidence supports the attention backend, tuned tiles and increasing
admission above 64. It does not establish an optimal trainer/engine split. Compare
longer runs with the same workload and objective, useful tokens per allocated GPU-hour,
policy age, stale/unused work and judge time before selecting a production topology.

### Recipe alignment

All three Small recipes, including mechanics, now use the Tiny learning baseline
from [PR #2271](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/pull/2271):

| Setting | Current Small baseline | Historical Small measurements |
|---|---|---|
| Prompts × responses per prompt | 256 × 8 | 128 × 8 |
| Responses per optimizer update | 2,048 | 1,024 |
| Learning rate | 6e-6, constant, no warmup | 1e-6, constant, no warmup |
| Loss weighting | Token mean | Response mean |
| Group-standard-deviation normalization | Off | Off |

This is the starting baseline for Small; the historical throughput results do not
measure this combination. The serving geometry remains the submitted timing4n/timing8
geometry. Paths, credentials, runtime budgets and mechanics qualification controls
also have the documented changes above.

The completed-buffer factor stays four: 1,024 prompt groups / 8,192 responses.
Unfinished producer budgets remain 672, 2,208 and 4,512 for the two/four/eight-node
layouts, respectively (0.328, 1.078 and 2.203 optimizer batches). The nominal sum
of unfinished budget plus completed-buffer capacity is therefore 4.328, 5.078 and
6.203 batches. Finished siblings can live outside that accounting; these figures
are not policy-age guarantees. Inspect measured age and useful throughput when
tuning the new baseline.
Do not copy Tiny's 12.5B inference preset, evaluator profile or cache geometry into
Small: those are model-specific. Checkpoint/export/evaluation differences here are
intentional for disposable timing runs, not a learning-run baseline.

- Trainer: ~6.9K tok/s/GPU at EP8 on 4 nodes; ~6.0K tok/s/GPU with 2 × EP8; about 8.6-8.9M
  model tokens per update.
- Response lengths are long: the median of per-update mean accepted lengths is about 8.1-8.4K
  tokens, truncation is 0-6%, and about 25% of groups are zero-std.
- Startup to the end of update 0: 1,953-2,429 s on 4 nodes, 1,543 s on 8 nodes.
- timing8 completed all 30 updates, then exited 1 at teardown because the final generation drain
  hit its 900 s timeout. Terminal refresh cleanup now cancels unused generation through
  the existing backend shutdown API before closing weight transport and disposing
  servers. This change has CPU runtime regression coverage; a clean Small GPU run
  is still required. Evaluation and final HF export retain their generation-drain
  boundaries because they may reuse live serving resources.

## What did not work or was not tested

- `fa4` attention: crashes on head_dim 256 (above).
- R=64: slower (396 vs 302 s/update); engines gain throughput up to R=96. In single-engine
  forced decodes, R=144 matched R=96 and R=192 gave +19% total tok/s with each request ~40%
  slower.
- EP4 trainer: untested.

## Code and runtime

The original timing runs needed no Small-specific adapter or weight-sync changes. timing4 ran on image
01M7A0QM57N9499PGFAT73SMF0 (open-instruct a87a0feac). timing4n and r64 ran on image
01M7GA94Q6GKMP2MV2N36YE83Q, built from open-instruct 5c6645da. That is main 28c18166 plus an
SGLang pin with an Olmo 3 sliding-window KV backport, which Small (no sliding-window layers)
does not use. `plan` on main resolves the timing4n config identically to 5c6645da. These
examples have not been run on an image built from main.

## Qualification before a learning run

Copy `two-node-mech.toml` to ignored `runs/`, set a fresh output path and the actual
workspace/secret names, then inspect `python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/small-mech.toml`
and `python -m open_instruct.miles validate runs/small-mech.toml` before using the
[committed-image launcher](launching.md). Build the image from the revision being
qualified; `plan` equality cannot establish runtime equality.

Retain the Beaker experiment link, image ID, submitted TOML and completion artifacts.
Verify all four updates, successful code grading, passing initial weight comparison,
standalone/training score agreement, publication acknowledgments and a clean exit.
Inspect `refresh_scores` for mixed-version responses and their historical-prefix and
latest-forward log-ratio diagnostics; see [Core diagnostics](core.md) and
[mixed-policy refresh](async-pipeline.md#mixed-policy-refresh). Those ratios include
policy drift and are not an isolated numerical-parity measurement.

For publication debugging, enable `core.diagnostic_interval = 1` with
`miles.check_weight_update_equal = true` in the run copy to exercise the existing
snapshot/reset/republish checks after optimizer updates. This adds a second transfer
and extra gradient/update diagnostics. The check detects incomplete transfers over
its selected tensors; it does not independently prove the export mapping. Keep a
separate Core-versus-serving score comparison on identical tokens, prefixes and
weights as a qualification requirement. HF-versus-SGLang greedy agreement and an
always-zero training metric do not establish that comparison.

Longer learning runs additionally need native checkpoint/save-resume and evaluation
checks. The historical timing runs disabled saving; the current four-/eight-node starters
enable bounded recovery saves. Their inputs still have no held-out split.

## Open items

- R160 finished 50 updates, then failed its 900-second final generation drain.
  It used server concurrency 320, 192 KDA slots, CUDA graph batch 160, producer
  budget 3,680 and an auto-sized KV pool. Repeat after the terminal-cleanup fix
  and under the intended code-grading and batch/loss configuration.
- Judge latency is not logged per call, so the judge's share of generation wait is unmeasured.
- The earlier claim that `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` is always zero was incorrect.
  Raw actor metric events record about 0.008 over the measured timing windows;
  `collection_score_mean_abs` is about 0.0065-0.0067. These combine numerical and
  policy differences; they do not replace a controlled same-weight parity check.

## Checkpoint settings in the current starters

The four- and eight-node templates now enable 10-update native recovery saves,
automatic resume, retention of the latest two saves and 50-update permanent
milestones, plus a final native save. Their 30-update starting budgets therefore
save at 10/20/30; 50-update retention becomes relevant when the run is extended.
The four-update two-node mechanics check still disables checkpoints/resume.
The reported historical timings used checkpoint-disabled runs and do not include
this new save overhead or qualify restore correctness. Measure current batch 2,048
wall time and checkpoint cost, aim for recovery saves roughly every 1–2 hours, and
verify the first save and resume before relying on these settings for long runs.
See [the shared checkpoint policy](../../configs/miles/examples/README.md#recovery-checkpoints-and-preserved-milestones).

# Development defaults

This page is light guidance from developing the MILES GRPO path. Each entry gives
a starting point and what to weigh when changing it. Unless an entry says
otherwise, a default is **not established as optimal, or even good**, for any
particular model, scale or task; it is simply where to begin. Where the
maintained example TOMLs encode a choice, the example is authoritative.
The demo configs are the baseline for configuration options unless otherwise
stated; document deviations in each experiment, including objective changes.

## Objective and data

The maintained examples enable final-answer grading with
`core.reward_final_answer_only=true` and `reward_reasoning_mode="required"`.
Use `"none"` explicitly for a non-thinking policy/template. The library default
remains false for compatibility with existing runs; see [grading contracts](grading.md).

- **Tiny learning batch and LR** (`node` and `three-node`): 256 prompts × 8 responses,
  batch 2,048 and constant learning rate 6e-6 with no warmup. The Tiny LR/batch
  exploration used response-mean loss; retaining the separately selected token-mean
  example objective is an engineering choice, not a measured combined optimum.
- **Policy lag** (12 in both `node` and `three-node`): a higher limit discards fewer slow groups but trains on older samples; reconsider it when learning rate, group size or response length changes.
- **Loss weighting** (token mean, `miles.calculate_per_token_loss = true`): keep the demo objective in throughput trials; response-mean loss is an explicit learning-policy override. Omitted library settings retain response-mean weighting for compatibility.
- **Off-policy correction** (TIS on, `use_rollout_logprobs = false`): TIS reweights samples toward the current policy; turning it off assumes inference and training probabilities agree closely.
- **Group filtering** (`training.filter_zero_std_groups = true`): groups where every response gets the same reward carry no policy gradient, so dropping them saves training work at the cost of extra generation; disable it for tiny checks that cannot produce mixed rewards.
- **Router auxiliary losses** (coefficients zero in the examples): the balancing and z-losses keep expert load even during pretraining; whether RL needs them is open, so watch the `train/moe/` load metrics if you leave them off.
- **Ungraded responses** (`core.exclude_ungraded = true`): a response whose verifier or judge failed for infrastructure reasons has no grade; it is left out of its group's baseline with zero advantage and a zeroed loss mask instead of being scored zero or taking its graded siblings down with it. See [the GRPO guide](grpo.md#ungraded-responses).
- **Truncated responses** (zero reward, `core.reward_zero_truncated = true`): responses that hit the length cap receive zero reward; this does not itself remove them from the training batch. Scoring them normally requires an explicit experiment override.

## Publication and capacity

- **Publication mode** (`refresh` for full-model async runs, `barrier` for small synchronous checks): refresh keeps generating across weight updates, so long responses span several policy versions; barrier is simpler to reason about but stalls generation at each update.
- **Engine admission** (generic default 64; the named `olmo35-b300-12.5@0.8` preset uses 512): size it from GPU memory, with `sglang_max_total_tokens = admission × context`; higher values add throughput only while memory and the router keep up. See the [example settings and limits](../../configs/miles/examples/README.md#capacity-and-qualification-settings) before transferring 512 to another model or GPU.
- **HTTP admission** (generic async default twice running admission; the named `olmo35-b300-12.5@0.8` preset uses 512/512): permits cover transit and response processing as well as generation. Additional permits can refill GPU slots or just add queueing; measure occupancy and residence time before increasing them.
- **Producer budget** (automatic when `async_max_concurrent_samples` is unset): the automatic value scales with the engine fleet; a larger budget fills engines more reliably but leaves more work to age out. The node example explicitly limits unfinished samples to 1,024. The three-node example explicitly limits unfinished samples to 3,840. These budgets are starting points for useful consumption, not targets for filling every reserved engine slot. The full three-node recipe can remain limited by collection and judging; validate sustained throughput and policy age before scaling the budget.
- **Completed buffer** (one collection by default and in `node`; four collections in `three-node`): separate from unfinished-request headroom; enlarging it retains more completed work without fixing response transport.
- **Submission granularity** (`"sample"`): engines refill as individual responses finish rather than waiting for whole groups.
- **Activation recomputation** (on for long contexts): trades extra compute for memory; turning it off is reasonable for short contexts once memory fit is checked.
- **Radix caching** (set by named presets: on for B300, off for H100; off for generic/colocated setups): the realistic-prompt comparison favored cached 512 on B300 and uncached 512 on H100. Presets are applied whole; use `inference.profile="generic"` and explicit settings to change cache mode. Cached hybrid serving needs the pinned FP32 tracked-state implementation; rebuild images after changing runtime pins. Recheck this choice for different prompt reuse and lengths.
- **Compiler cache** (on): shortens repeat startup and does not change training.
- **Weight equality audit** (off in learning templates, on in mechanics templates): startup snapshot/reset qualification is separate from the required publication protocol.
- **Trainer scoring** (`scoring_pass_required = false`): reuse the training forward only when the recipe permits it. Learning templates set `scoring_check_interval = 0` to retain startup/resume validation without periodic extra scoring forwards; TIS and required scoring remain active.
- **Native checkpoints** (every10 updates in the learning starters): aim for roughly 1–2 hours between ephemeral recovery saves, using measured wall-clock update and save times. Retain the latest two saves, permanent 50-/100-update milestones as specified by the template, and the final checkpoint. Include startup/compilation and evaluation overhead when checking that the first complete save fits comfortably inside protected runtime. Verify actual saving, bounded retention and restored optimizer/cursor identity; automatic restart alone is not recovery. See [the template checkpoint policy](../../configs/miles/examples/README.md#recovery-checkpoints-and-preserved-milestones).

## Opt-in features

- **Expert-aware packing** (off): may reduce MoE load imbalance, but planning cost can cancel the savings; measure end-to-end update time before adopting it.
- **FP32 output head** (off): reduces probability mismatch between training and serving at some memory cost; its effect on learning is unknown.
- **Engine drain** (off): an experimental alternative to refresh that finishes requests before swapping weights; no example uses it.

9	stated; document deviations in each experiment, including objective changes.
10	
11	## Objective and data
12	
13	The maintained examples enable final-answer grading with
14	`core.reward_final_answer_only=true` and `reward_reasoning_mode="required"`.
15	Use `"none"` explicitly for a non-thinking policy/template. The library default
16	remains false for compatibility with existing runs; see [grading contracts](grading.md).
17	
18	- **Tiny learning batch and LR** (`node` and `three-node`): 256 prompts × 8 responses,
19	  batch 2,048 and constant learning rate 6e-6 with no warmup. The Tiny LR/batch
20	  exploration used response-mean loss; retaining the separately selected token-mean
21	  example objective is an engineering choice, not a measured combined optimum.
22	- **Policy lag** (12 in both `node` and `three-node`): a higher limit discards fewer slow groups but trains on older samples; reconsider it when learning rate, group size or response length changes.
23	- **Loss weighting** (token mean, `miles.calculate_per_token_loss = true`): keep the demo objective in throughput trials; response-mean loss is an explicit learning-policy override. Omitted library settings retain response-mean weighting for compatibility.
24	- **Off-policy correction** (TIS on, `use_rollout_logprobs = false`): TIS reweights samples toward the current policy; turning it off assumes inference and training probabilities agree closely.
25	- **Group filtering** (`training.filter_zero_std_groups = true`): groups where every response gets the same reward carry no policy gradient, so dropping them saves training work at the cost of extra generation; disable it for tiny checks that cannot produce mixed rewards.
26	- **Router auxiliary losses** (coefficients zero in the examples): the balancing and z-losses keep expert load even during pretraining; whether RL needs them is open, so watch the `train/moe/` load metrics if you leave them off.
27	- **Ungraded responses** (`core.exclude_ungraded = true`): a response whose verifier or judge failed for infrastructure reasons has no grade; it is left out of its group's baseline with zero advantage and a zeroed loss mask instead of being scored zero or taking its graded siblings down with it. See [the GRPO guide](grpo.md#ungraded-responses).
28	- **Truncated responses** (zero reward, `core.reward_zero_truncated = true`): responses that hit the length cap receive zero reward; this does not itself remove them from the training batch. Scoring them normally requires an explicit experiment override.
29	
30	## Publication and capacity
31	
32	- **Publication mode** (`refresh` for full-model async runs, `barrier` for small synchronous checks): refresh keeps generating across weight updates, so long responses span several policy versions; barrier is simpler to reason about but stalls generation at each update.
33	- **Engine admission** (generic default 64; the named `olmo35-b300-12.5@0.8` preset uses 512): size it from GPU memory, with `sglang_max_total_tokens = admission × context`; higher values add throughput only while memory and the router keep up. See the [example settings and limits](../../configs/miles/examples/README.md#capacity-and-qualification-settings) before transferring 512 to another model or GPU.
34	- **HTTP admission** (generic async default twice running admission; the named `olmo35-b300-12.5@0.8` preset uses 512/512): permits cover transit and response processing as well as generation. Additional permits can refill GPU slots or just add queueing; measure occupancy and residence time before increasing them.
35	- **Producer budget** (automatic when `async_max_concurrent_samples` is unset): the automatic value scales with the engine fleet; a larger budget fills engines more reliably but leaves more work to age out. The node example explicitly limits unfinished samples to 1,024. The three-node example explicitly limits unfinished samples to 3,840. These budgets are starting points for useful consumption, not targets for filling every reserved engine slot. The full three-node recipe can remain limited by collection and judging; validate sustained throughput and policy age before scaling the budget.
36	- **Completed buffer** (one collection by default and in `node`; four collections in `three-node`): separate from unfinished-request headroom; enlarging it retains more completed work without fixing response transport.
37	- **Submission granularity** (`"sample"`): engines refill as individual responses finish rather than waiting for whole groups.
38	- **Activation recomputation** (on for long contexts): trades extra compute for memory; turning it off is reasonable for short contexts once memory fit is checked.
39	- **Radix caching** (set by named presets: on for B300, off for H100; off for generic/colocated setups): the realistic-prompt comparison favored cached 512 on B300 and uncached 512 on H100. Presets are applied whole; use `inference.profile="generic"` and explicit settings to change cache mode. Cached hybrid serving needs the pinned FP32 tracked-state implementation; rebuild images after changing runtime pins. Recheck this choice for different prompt reuse and lengths.
40	- **Compiler cache** (on): shortens repeat startup and does not change training.
41	- **Weight equality audit** (off in learning templates, on in mechanics templates): startup snapshot/reset qualification is separate from the required publication protocol.
42	- **Trainer scoring** (`scoring_pass_required = false`): reuse the training forward only when the recipe permits it. Learning templates set `scoring_check_interval = 0` to retain startup/resume validation without periodic extra scoring forwards; TIS and required scoring remain active.

Retain the latest two saves, permanent 50-/100-update milestones as specified by the template, and the final checkpoint. Include startup/compilation and evaluation overhead when checking that the first complete save fits comfortably inside protected runtime. Verify actual saving, bounded retention and restored optimizer/cursor identity; automatic restart alone is not recovery. See [the template checkpoint policy](../../configs/miles/examples/README.md#recovery-checkpoints-and-preserved-milestones).

45	## Opt-in features
46	
47	- **Expert-aware packing** (off): may reduce MoE load imbalance, but planning cost can cancel the savings; measure end-to-end update time before adopting it.
48	- **FP32 output head** (off): reduces probability mismatch between training and serving at some memory cost; its effect on learning is unknown.
49	- **Engine drain** (off): an experimental alternative to refresh that finishes requests before swapping weights; no example uses it.

# u8-l1 MILES 总览与架构分层

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说出 MILES 与 `grpo.py`（Core/vLLM）、`grpo_fast.py`（DeepSpeed/vLLM）三条 RL 训练路线的关系与各自适用范围。
2. 理解 MILES 的所有权分层：open-instruct 包装层负责什么、MILES 运行时负责什么、Core 适配器经 OLMo-core 与 SGLang 又负责什么。
3. 会用 `python -m open_instruct.miles` 的五个子命令（`plan` / `validate` / `train` / `run` / `status`）以及 `records` 记录分析工具。
4. 知道维护示例按模型家族组织在 `configs/miles/examples/tiny/` 与 `configs/miles/examples/small/` 下：tiny 家族是力学/学习示例，small 家族在上一轮（PR #2280）从 dev 占位副本升级为实测的 OLMo 3.5 Small（A4B）B300 三档配方（two-node-mech / four-node / eight-node），且全部维护示例的损失基线已翻转为 token-mean（PR #2271）。
5. 掌握本轮（PR #2289，提交 27f868159）固化的**学习示例恢复保存基线**：Tiny node/three-node 与 Small four/eight-node 统一为每 10 更新保存、保留最近 2 份、外加 50/100 更新里程碑与最终存档，Small four/eight-node 从「禁用保存、不自动恢复」翻转为启用；本轮 #2293 还把 Small 三份配方的心跳超时从 120 升到 480 秒、MILES 运行时 pin 升至 9eff46a4。
6. 了解文档地图的扩展脉络：`grading.md` 与 `abstention.md`（上一轮）、`olmo35-small.md`（上一轮）及其本轮新增的「Checkpoint settings in the current starters」一节，以及 examples README 本轮新增的「Recovery checkpoints and preserved milestones」共享策略节。

本讲是 MILES 单元（u8）的第一篇，只做总览不深入细节；配置系统、工作流执行、奖励体系分别在 u8-l2、u8-l3、u8-l6 及之后各讲展开，Small B300 配方的显存账目与吞吐审计另立一讲（u8-l15）。

## 2. 前置知识

阅读本讲前，建议先具备以下概念（不熟悉也没关系，下面用通俗语言解释）：

- **RLVR / GRPO**：可验证奖励强化学习（RL with Verifiable Rewards）。对数学题、代码这类有标准答案的任务，可以用一个「验证器」自动判分作为奖励，而不需要训练额外的奖励模型。GRPO 是一种组相对策略优化算法：对同一个 prompt 采样一组回答，按组内奖励的相对高低计算优势。已在 u6-l1、u6-l2 讲过。
- **rollout（rollout 编排）**：RL 训练的一步是「让当前策略生成一批回答 → 判分 → 用结果更新策略」。生成这批回答的过程及其调度（队列、准入、引擎管理）称为 rollout 编排。
- **Ray actor**：Ray 分布式框架中的常驻进程，持有 GPU 资源并响应远程调用。MILES 运行时用 Ray actor 承载训练器与推理引擎。
- **OLMo-core 与 SGLang**：OLMo-core 是 Allen AI 的模型与分布式训练库（提供模型结构、checkpoint、分布式原语）；SGLang 是推理服务框架。MILES 用前者训练、后者服务。
- **TOML run 文件**：MILES 用一个结构化 TOML 文件描述一次完整运行（模型、数据、拓扑、启动、追踪等），是所有子命令的输入。
- **token-mean 与 response-mean 损失加权**：一个批次里有长有短的回答。response-mean（按响应平均）给每个回答同等权重，长回答里的每个 token 影响被稀释；token-mean（按 token 平均，`calculate_per_token_loss=true`）给每个 token 同等权重。维护示例统一采用 token-mean，但省略该设置时库默认仍是 response-mean，以兼容既有 run。
- **有界恢复保存与永久里程碑（bounded recovery saves / preserved milestones）**：RL 训练一次运行数小时到数天，被抢占或中断后要能从最近的完整存档恢复。「有界」指普通恢复保存滚动保留最近 N 份（磁盘占用不随时间无限增长）；「里程碑」（`checkpoint_keep_every`）指每隔更长的更新间隔**永久**保留一份，供扩展运行与事后回溯；另有 `save_final_checkpoint` 在结束时落最终存档。本轮 #2289 把学习型模板统一到「每 10 更新保存、保留最近 2 份、50 或 100 更新里程碑 + 最终存档」。
- **心跳超时（heartbeat_timeout）与受保护最短运行时（min_runtime）**：Beaker 集群上驱动进程靠心跳向监控证明自己还活着，超时（本轮 Small 配方从 120 秒升至 480 秒）会被判定为僵死；`min_runtime` 是调度器保证分配的受保护时长。恢复保存的节奏必须与这两者配合——首个完整恢复保存应落在受保护时长之内。
- **B300 与 MoE**：B300 是 NVIDIA 的 Blackwell Ultra 数据中心 GPU（AI2 的 Holmes 集群使用）；MoE（混合专家）模型每个 token 只激活部分专家参数。OLMo 3.5 Small（A4B）是 256 专家、约 0.8B 激活参数的小型 MoE 模型。
- **Beaker**：AI2 的实验平台，MILES 的 `run` 子命令把 TOML 编译成 Beaker 实验提交。不熟悉 Beaker 也不影响本讲，详见 u8-l8。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 CLI 入口：`python -m open_instruct.miles`

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

MILES 在 open-instruct 中的公开入口只有一条命令：`python -m open_instruct.miles`。它把「规划、校验、本地执行、Beaker 提交、状态查询」以及「推理记录分析」全部收拢到一个入口后面。

为什么这样设计？

- **研究者的全部意图浓缩在一个 TOML run 文件里**。同一条命令对不同子命令复用同一份配置，避免「训练用一套脚本、提交用另一套脚本」的漂移。
- **运行时导入是延迟的**。GPU/MILES 运行时只在真正需要的子命令里才 import，因此 `plan` / `validate` 这类规划命令在没有 GPU、没有安装 MILES 私有运行时的笔记本电脑上也能运行。这一点是文档明确承诺的：[docs/miles/index.md:L21-L23](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/docs/miles/index.md#L21-L23) 写明 "Planning does not require GPUs or mounted checkpoints"。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

CLI 的一次执行流程：

```text
python -m open_instruct.miles COMMAND CONFIG.toml [--set SECTION.KEY=VALUE ...]
        │
        ├─ sys.argv[1] == "records"？
        │    ├─ "select"        → open_instruct.miles.datasets.record_selection
        │    ├─ "replay-pool"   → open_instruct.miles.datasets.replay_summary
        │    └─ 其他            → miles.utils.record_summary（需 MILES 运行时）
        │
        └─ 否则：argparse 解析 COMMAND ∈ {plan, validate, train, run, status}
             │
             ├─ 读取 TOML → payload
             ├─ 判断结构化：payload 含 schema_version 或 model 字段？
             │    ├─ 是 → specs.from_dict(...) 解析为 RunSpec（结构化 run 文件）
             │    └─ 否 → RunConfig.from_dict(...)（低层原始配置）
             │
             └─ 按命令分发：
                  plan     → config.plan()，打印计划 JSON + 提示（advisories）
                  validate → 结构化：plan() 全量校验；原始：parse_runtime()
                  run      → execution.launch.run()（提交 Beaker，仅限结构化）
                  status   → execution.launch.status()（仅限结构化）
                  train    → workflow.execute(config)（结构化）/ train_config（原始）
                             （OPDRunSpec 走独立的 distillation.opd_runtime 路径）
```

注意两个设计点：

1. **结构化 run 文件与低层配置双轨**。`run`/`status` 只接受 `schema_version=1` 的结构化文件；低层原始配置只支持 `plan`/`validate`/`train`。这让「研究者视角的完整 run」与「底层调参视角的 CoreConfig」都能进门，但提交必须走结构化路线。
2. **错误处理友好**。输入错误（`InputError`）默认被转成一行 `parser.error` 提示而不是一长串 traceback，加 `--debug` 才展开。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

> 近两轮提交（#2271/#2280/#2286 与本轮 #2289/#2293）均未改动此文件，行号与上一版讲义一致。

模块 docstring 即是命令速查，明确写出五个子命令与 records 的用法：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L1-L12](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L1-L12)。其中 L4-L5 说明「运行时导入延迟到需要它的命令，规划无需 GPU 栈」这一关键约束。

`main()` 的第一步先拦截 `records` 分支，按子命令名选择实现模块；若缺 `miles` 包则给出「需在锁定运行时中运行」的退出提示：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L26-L44](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L26-L44)。这段代码同时示范了「延迟导入」模式——`importlib.import_module` 只在确定目标后才执行。

主解析器只有三个位置参数：命令、配置路径与可重复的 `--set` 覆盖：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L45-L57](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L45-L57)。L46 的 `choices=("plan", "validate", "train", "run", "status")` 就是「五个子命令」的出处。

`execute()` 读取 TOML 文档后，用 `schema_version in payload or "model" in payload` 判定结构化与否，再分别构造 `RunSpec`（经 `specs.from_dict`）或 `RunConfig`：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L66-L73](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L66-L73)。这是「TOML → RunSpec → RunConfig」编译链的入口（编译链细节在 u8-l2 精读）。

`plan` 分支调用 `config.plan()` 并打印 JSON 与 advisories，不做任何 GPU 操作：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L74-L78](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L74-L78)。

`run`/`status` 要求结构化文件并延迟导入 `execution.launch`：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L79-L87](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L79-L87)。L81 的报错信息直接写明「raw configs support plan/validate/train」。

`validate` 与 `train` 的分发：结构化校验会连物理分配一起 `plan()`，而训练交给 `workflow.execute`（细节在 u8-l3）：[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L96-L109](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L96-L109)。OPD（蒸馏）规格有独立分支（L88-L95），本讲不展开。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：在无 GPU、无 MILES 运行时的机器上，用 `plan` 验证一份维护示例配置，体会「规划不需要 GPU 栈」。

**操作步骤**：

1. 在仓库根目录执行（open-instruct 用 uv 管理依赖，见 u1-l2）：

   ```bash
   uv run python -m open_instruct.miles plan configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml
   ```

2. 观察输出的 JSON 计划（包含解析后的拓扑、批次几何与编译选项）以及 advisories 提示。
3. 再试一次带覆盖的规划，观察字段被就地替换：

   ```bash
   uv run python -m open_instruct.miles plan configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml \
     --set training.num_rollouts=2
   ```

4. 故意打错命令名验证 argparse 的 choices 约束：

   ```bash
   uv run python -m open_instruct.miles plans configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml
   ```

**需要观察的现象**：步骤 1/2 输出计划 JSON 与提示；步骤 3 中 `training.num_rollouts` 从模板里的 4 变为 2；步骤 4 报 `invalid choice` 错误并列出五个合法命令。

**预期结果**：`plan` 只做 CPU 侧的配置解析与物理分配规划，不触发 GPU 运行时导入；本讲撰写时未在本地实际执行该命令，输出样例**待本地验证**（文档承诺见 [docs/miles/index.md:L21-L23](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/docs/miles/index.md#L21-L23)）。注意：模板中的 `/weka/.../YOUR_USERNAME/...` 是占位路径，个别校验可能对其报提示，属正常现象；`plan` 不要求挂载这些路径。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `run`/`status` 拒绝低层原始配置（`RunConfig`），只接受 `schema_version=1` 的结构化文件？

**参考答案**：`run` 要把「模型、数据、拓扑、启动、挂载」完整编译成 Beaker 实验，这些信息只有结构化 RunSpec 才齐备；低层 `RunConfig` 只描述训练器参数，缺少提交所需的 launch/output 等段落。源码在 [open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L79-L81](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L79-L81) 显式报错。

**练习 2**：`python -m open_instruct.miles records summarize` 与 `plan` 对运行环境的依赖有何不同？

**参考答案**：`records summarize` 分发到 MILES 包内的 `miles.utils.record_summary`，需要安装 MILES 私有运行时（缺失时报「requires the MILES package」）；`plan` 只依赖 open-instruct 的 CPU 配置代码，无需 GPU 栈。见 [open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L27-L44](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L27-L44)。

**练习 3**：`--set name=my-run` 这样的覆盖发生在哪个阶段？与直接改 TOML 有何区别？

**参考答案**：覆盖作为 `overrides` 参数传给 `specs.from_dict` / `RunConfig.from_dict`（[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L69-L73](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L69-L73)），在解析时叠加到 TOML 文档之上。区别：TOML 文件保持原样（可继续作为版本化的基准），覆盖只影响这一次调用，适合临时调参、sweep 与调试。

### 4.2 架构分层：三层所有权与适配器包布局

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

MILES 不是「又一个训练脚本」，而是把一次 RL 运行拆给三个所有者：

- **open-instruct 包装层**：研究者面对的一切——配置校验、数据准备、验证器/奖励、Beaker 提交与回执、运行产物。
- **MILES 运行时**（私有、按锁定制）：rollout actor、SGLang 推理引擎、采样/优势/损失机制、共享传输。
- **Core 适配器**（位于 MILES 内）：模型构建、打分与训练前向、梯度同步、优化器与 checkpoint、权重导出；训练走 OLMo-core，服务走 SGLang。

为什么要有这条边界？因为 open-instruct 是公开研究仓库，而 MILES 运行时（含其 pinned fork）是独立发布的私有组件。open-instruct 负责「研究者想要什么」，MILES 负责「RL 机制怎么做」，Core 适配器负责「在 OLMo-core 上真正训练」。理解这条边界后，你在 open-instruct 仓库里看到的每个 `open_instruct/miles/` 子包都能归位到某一层。

同时要记住：**MILES 不取代既有 GRPO 训练器**。`grpo.py`（Core/vLLM）与 `grpo_fast.py`（DeepSpeed/vLLM，u6-l4 讲过其 Ray 拓扑）仍是稠密模型训练与历史复现的现行选择；MILES 面向受支持的 Olmo MoE 模型（也提供稠密 Olmo 3 适配器，但验证较少）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

一次 MILES 运行的纵向视角：

```text
研究者编写 run.toml（schema_version=1）
        │  python -m open_instruct.miles plan / validate      ← open-instruct：CPU 校验与规划
        ▼
RunSpec ──编译──▶ RunConfig（含 CoreConfig 与原生 MILES 选项）
        │  python -m open_instruct.miles run                  ← open-instruct：编译 Beaker 实验并提交
        ▼
Beaker 上的应用镜像（按 runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json 构建）
        │
        ▼
MILES 运行时启动：Ray 集群、裁判加载、工作流准备并发启动
        │
        ▼
Core 适配器（OLMoCoreTrainRayActor）：SGLang 服务策略 → rollout → 打分 →
OLMo-core 训练前向/反向 → 权重发布（refresh/barrier/engine_drain）→ checkpoint/导出
```

分层所有权表（五层，前三层是所有权划分，后两层是上游基座）：

| 层 | 拥有 |
|---|---|
| Open Instruct 包装层 | 配置校验、准备、验证器、提交/回执、运行产物 |
| MILES 运行时 | rollout actor、SGLang 引擎、采样/优势/损失机制、共享传输助手 |
| Core 适配器（在 MILES 中） | 模型构建、文档/回放对齐、打分与训练前向、梯度同步、优化器/checkpoint、张量导出 |
| OLMo-core | 模型与分布式训练原语、注意力/专家执行 |
| olmo-sglang | 服务架构注册与模型专属执行 |

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：MILES 与 `grpo_fast.py` 都用 Ray + 多进程做 RL，本质区别是什么？

**参考答案**：`grpo_fast.py` 是 open-instruct 仓库内的一个完整训练脚本（DeepSpeed 训练器 + vLLM 引擎，代码全部在本仓库，u6-l4）；MILES 把「rollout 编排与共享 RL 机制」交给私有 MILES 运行时（按 `runtime.lock.json` 锁定），open-instruct 只保留配置/数据/奖励集成与提交，训练走 OLMo-core、服务走 SGLang。另见 [docs/miles/index.md:L8-L13](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/docs/miles/index.md#L8-L13)：引入 MILES 不弃用既有 GRPO 训练器。

**练习 2**：如果要在 MILES 训练中新增一种自定义验证器，改动应落在哪一层？为什么？

**参考答案**：落在 open-instruct 包装层的 `open_instruct/miles/rewards/`（验证器、奖励路由与托管裁判），以可信注册表条目（factory + 配置）暴露给 MILES。因为后端训练器与托管 rollout 模块不导入 open-instruct（[docs/miles/architecture.md:L304-L313](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/docs/miles/architecture.md#L304-L313)），MILES 侧只通过约定路径消费应用侧回调与注册表。（验证器细节见 u8-l6。）

**练习 3**：为什么 open-instruct 的普通 `uv.lock` 环境跑不了 MILES 训练，而 `plan` 却能跑？本轮运行时锁前进后，旧镜像还能继续用吗？

**参考答案**：训练需要 MILES 私有运行时、SGLang 与锁定版本的 OLMo-core，这些由 `runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json` 与专用应用镜像提供（[docs/miles/architecture.md:L25-L30](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/docs/miles/architecture.md#L25-L30)、[docs/miles/architecture.md:L179-L193](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/docs/miles/architecture.md#L179-L193)）；`plan` 只走 CPU 配置代码，CLI 把运行时 import 延迟到需要它的命令（[open_instruct/miles/__main__.py:L4-L5](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/open_instruct/miles/__main__.py#L4-L5)）。旧镜像不可靠：锁的 revision 已从 22d2fb4c 升到 9eff46a4（[runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json:L13-L16](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/runtime/miles/runtime.lock.json#L13-L16)），examples README 明确提醒 launcher 只核对镜像 ID、不核对镜像内源码是否匹配当前锁，应核对镜像构建记录或直接重建（[configs/miles/examples/README.md:L83-L91](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/configs/miles/examples/README.md#L83-L91)）。

**参考答案**：不对。`configuration.md` 等生成式参考页由 MkDocs 从配置源在内存中生成、不入库；应编辑源定义与审校描述，再用 `python -m scripts.miles.generate_docs` 重新生成、`--check` 校验。见 [docs/miles/index.md:L55-L63](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/docs/miles/index.md#L55-L63)。

**参考答案**：首页表格是按「什么时候用」组织的精选主表，面向通用工作流；olmo35-small.md 是特定模型（OLMo 3.5 Small）+ 特定硬件（B300）的实测记录，读者群更窄。它经由 mkdocs 站点导航的 "Models and training" 组接入（[mkdocs.yml:L110](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/mkdocs.yml#L110)），并被 `configs/miles/examples/README.md` 与 small 配方文件的注释引用。检索文档时不能只看首页表。

**练习 3**：`core.reward_final_answer_only` 的库默认值与维护示例值分别是什么？为什么示例要显式写出？

**参考答案**：库默认 `false`（保留历史判分行为），维护示例显式设 `true`（思考型策略只判交付响应）。示例是配置基线——除非 run 明确声明，应以示例为准，显式写出避免「沉默改变目标」。见 [docs/miles/grading.md:L7-L12](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/docs/miles/grading.md#L7-L12) 与 [configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml:L71-L77](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml#L71-L77)。

### 4.4 示例家族划分：tiny 与 small

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

维护示例（maintained examples）是 MILES 的「配置基线」：除非 run 明确声明，应以示例为准。示例按**模型家族**重组为 `tiny/` 与 `small/` 两个目录，近两轮这两个家族的分工与基线发生了两次实质变化：

- **tiny 家族**：微型模型的力学/学习示例——`dev.toml`（单 GPU 共置力学检查）、`node.toml`（单节点学习）、`three-node.toml`（三节点学习 + 后台评估）。上一轮统一了 Tiny 学习基线：256 prompts × 8 responses、batch 2048、恒定 LR 6e-6 无 warmup、token-mean loss；本轮 #2289 又统一了恢复保存基线：每 10 更新保存、保留最近 2 份、node 按 50 更新留里程碑（与既有的 50 更新开发面板对齐）、three-node 按 100 更新留里程碑，外加最终存档。
- **small 家族**：上一轮删除 `small/dev.toml` 占位，换成**实测的 OLMo 3.5 Small（A4B，KDA + 256 专家 MoE）B300 三档配方**：`two-node-mech.toml`（两节点力学检查，4 次更新，仍不保存 checkpoint）、`four-node.toml` 与 `eight-node.toml`（30 更新起步预算布局，本轮从「禁用保存、不自动恢复」翻转为启用与 Tiny 相同的有界恢复保存 + `auto_resume = true`）。

同时，**全部维护示例的损失基线从 per-response 翻转为 token-mean**：`miles.calculate_per_token_loss = true`。注意省略该设置时库默认仍是 `false`（response-mean），这是为兼容既有 run 而刻意保留的——所以每个示例都把它显式写出。

为什么按模型家族分目录？因为 serving 几何、显存账目、准入参数都是模型专属的：Small 文档明确告诫「不要把 Tiny 的 12.5B 推理 preset、评估 profile 或缓存几何复制进 Small」。

本轮还有一个容易被忽略的运维细节：#2293 把三份 Small 配方的 `heartbeat_timeout` 从 120 秒升到 480 秒——启用恢复保存与自动重启后，保存/恢复期间驱动可能长时间不发包，过紧的心跳会被误判为僵死（恢复语义详见 u8-l3）。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

当前六份维护示例的分工（与 README 表格一致，最后一列是本轮 #2289 固化的恢复保存基线）：

| 配置 | 家族 | 用途 | 恢复保存基线 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tiny/dev.toml` | tiny | 单 GPU、训练/推理共置；GSM8K 短力学检查 | 独立短跑设置（保留原样） |
| `tiny/node.toml` | tiny | 单个 8 GPU 节点：2 训练 GPU（EP2）+ 6 推理引擎；无裁判 | 每 10 更新；保留 2 份 + 50 更新里程碑 + 最终存档 |
| `tiny/three-node.toml` | tiny | 三节点学习：8 训练 GPU（EP8）、15 推理引擎 + 1 裁判；24 GPU，另加后台评估 | 每 10 更新；保留 2 份 + 100 更新里程碑 + 最终存档 |
| `small/two-node-mech.toml` | small | OLMo 3.5 Small 力学检查：8 训练 GPU（EP8）、7 引擎、1 裁判；4 次更新 | 不保存、不自动恢复（保持不变） |
| `small/four-node.toml` | small | Small 起步预算布局：8 训练 GPU（EP8）、23 引擎（R=96）、1 裁判；审计中位数约 302 s/更新 | 每 10 更新；保留 2 份 + 50 里程碑 + 最终存档；`auto_resume = true` |
| `small/eight-node.toml` | small | Small 起步预算布局：16 训练 GPU（2 × EP8）、47 引擎（R=96）、1 裁判；晚期窗口中位数约 185 s/更新 | 同 four-node |

近两轮基线变化的要点：

```text
损失加权（上一轮 #2271）：
            per-response（response-mean）      →  token-mean（calculate_per_token_loss = true）
           （省略该设置时库默认仍为 response-mean，兼容既有 run）

Tiny 学习（上一轮 #2271）：
            128 prompts × 8，batch 1024        →  256 prompts × 8，batch 2048
学习率：    （模板未显式设置）                  →  learning_rate = 6e-6，恒定、无 warmup

small 家族（上一轮 #2280）：
            small/dev.toml（tiny dev 的占位副本）→  三份实测 B300 配方 + docs/miles/olmo35-small.md
                                                +  configs/miles/moe_configs/（fused-MoE tile 调优）

学习示例恢复保存（本轮 #2289）：
            Tiny 学习模板 save_interval = 25    →  save_interval = 10 + checkpoint_keep_last = 2
                                                    + checkpoint_keep_every（node/Small=50，three-node=100）
                                                    + save_final_checkpoint = true
            Small four/eight-node：              →  启用上述保存基线 + auto_resume = true
            save_checkpoints = false、auto_resume = false

心跳超时（本轮 #2293）：
            Small 三份配方 heartbeat_timeout     →  480 秒（原 120 秒）
```

两个容易踩的陷阱：

1. **历史上的 Small 吞吐计时用的是旧设置**（batch 1024、LR 1e-6、response-mean，且未启用 code grading），且全部是**关闭保存**的运行——不含保存 I/O 开销。新基线（含每 10 更新的保存）不可直接沿用旧数字。
2. **里程碑间隔是「为扩展预留」的**：30 更新起步预算下，50/100 里程碑不会在本次运行内触发；它们只在把 `num_rollouts` 扩大后才生效。README 因此提醒：无 checkpoint 的计时实验要显式关掉保存与自动恢复并删掉 `save_interval`，且不要把该覆盖带进学习 run。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`tiny/` 与 `small/` 两个家族各自的分工是什么？为什么 Small 没有单 GPU 训练配方？

**参考答案**：`tiny/` 是 Tiny 微型模型的力学检查（dev）与学习示例（node/three-node）；`small/` 是实测的 OLMo 3.5 Small（A4B）B300 布局：two-node-mech 做力学检查，four/eight-node 做起步预算布局。Small 没有单 GPU 训练配方、两节点（8 训练 GPU + 7 引擎 + 1 裁判）是其最小已测配置——见 [configs/miles/examples/README.md:L17-L19](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/configs/miles/examples/README.md#L17-L19)。

**练习 2**：示例都写了 `calculate_per_token_loss = true`，为什么库默认仍是 `false`？这两者矛盾吗？

**参考答案**：不矛盾。库默认保留 response-mean 是为了兼容既有 run——省略该设置的老配置行为不变；维护示例显式设 `true` 是把新基线写清楚，避免「沉默改变目标」。development-defaults 同样写明「Omitted library settings retain response-mean weighting for compatibility」（Loss weighting 条目，其上一条即 Tiny learning batch and LR）：[docs/miles/development-defaults.md:L18-L23](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/docs/miles/development-defaults.md#L18-L23)。

**练习 3**：Small four/eight-node 的 30 更新预算下，保存点落在哪里？50 更新里程碑有什么用？为什么 README 要求「首个完整恢复保存应落在受保护最短运行时之内」？

**参考答案**：`save_interval = 10` 且启用最终存档，30 更新预算在 10/20/30 三处保存；`checkpoint_keep_every = 50` 在本次起步预算内不会触发，它是为把 `num_rollouts` 扩大后的长运行预留的永久里程碑（见 [docs/miles/olmo35-small.md:L235-L238](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/docs/miles/olmo35-small.md#L235-L238)）。受保护最短运行时是调度器保证的连续执行窗口：若首个完整保存来不及在窗口内落盘，一次抢占就会让整个 run 从零开始，恢复保存形同虚设；因此间隔要从实测墙钟时间选（目标约 1-2 小时一次，Tiny seed17 约 5-7 分钟/更新即约 50-70 分钟/10 更新），放不进就缩短间隔或修改预算（[configs/miles/examples/README.md:L341-L356](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/configs/miles/examples/README.md#L341-L356)）。另注意历史 Small 计时是关闭保存的运行，不含保存 I/O 开销，不能直接当作当前配方的 checkpoint 预测。

## 5. 综合实践

**任务：为你的第一次 MILES 冒烟运行制作一页「所有权笔记」，并在 tiny 与 small 两个家族之间做出正确选择。**

1. **复制模板**：把 [configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/configs/miles/examples/tiny/dev.toml) 复制到被 git 忽略的 `runs/my-dev.toml`（目录不存在则创建；不要直接改模板——配置约定见 [docs/miles/grpo.md:L42-L49](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/docs/miles/grpo.md#L42-L49)）。
2. **改占位符**：替换 `YOUR_USERNAME` 与模型/输出路径（README 的准备步骤见 [configs/miles/examples/README.md:L55-L70](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct/blob/2063f854b37cd380e55f5509df7ea50b6d8a1033/configs/miles/examples/README.md#L55-L70)）。
3. **无 GPU 规划**：运行 `uv run python -m open_instruct.miles plan runs/my-dev.toml`，把输出 JSON 里你认识的段落（model/data/training/inference/core）与 4.2 节架构图逐一连线。

5. **写一页笔记**，回答三个问题：
